articles.title: ¿Se cancela 'Barbie 2'? Un conflicto salarial pone en jaque el futuro de la saga
articles.text:
El futuro de Barbie 2, la secuela de la aclamada película dirigida por Greta Gerwig y protagonizada por Margot Robbie y Ryan Gosling, pende de un hilo. Según reporta Variety, el cuarteto creativo detrás de la película, que también incluye a Noah Baumbach, quien coescribió el guion de cinta original junto a Gerwig, su esposa, todavía no se pone de acuerdo por sus salarios con Warner Bros. Esto ha desatado una carrera contra el tiempo con el potencial de poner en jaque no solo la realización de un segundo largometraje, sino cualquier proyecto futuro vinculado con esta versión de la saga.
El estudio habría realizado más de seis ofertas económicas al equipo que componen Robbie, Gerwig, Gosling y Baumbach para concretar Barbie 2. Sin embargo, estos supuestamente las rechazaron por considerarlas insuficientes. La negativa habría desatado la ira de David Zaslav, CEO de Warner Bros, quien consideraría excesivas sus exigencias. Así, las negociaciones se habrían estancado, dejando la segunda película al borde de caer en el basurero.
Los comentarios de insiders respecto de esta disputa salarial por Barbie 2 son un tanto contradictorios. Variety indica que algunas de sus fuentes hablan de un ofrecimiento económico como Warner nunca antes hizo. Otras afirman que el número grupal es grande, pero que no contenta las expectativas de compensación individual de cada uno de los involucrados.
Puntualmente, se menciona que Ryan Gosling pretendería 20 millones de dólares para regresar como Ken. Margot Robbie y Greta Gerwig apuntarían a cifras bastante más altas que las que lograron con la primera Barbie, que de por sí fueron abultadas. Incluso se da a entender que la actriz australiana habría embolsado más de 50 millones de dólares por el filme original.
Sea como sea, el panorama no parece demasiado benévolo para la concreción de Barbie 2. No solo porque ni los responsables de la película ni el jefe del estudio darían el brazo a torcer con sus respectivas posiciones. También, porque los derechos de Warner para hacer la secuela estarían por vencer.
El futuro de Barbie 2, con Margot Robbie, pende de un hilo
Warner Bros tiene los derechos para hacer una secuela de Barbie hasta dentro de cuatro meses. Si el proyecto no avanza dentro de ese lapso de tiempo, esos derechos volverán a manos de Mattel. Aquí la historia se complica incluso más. En caso de darse esta situación la juguetera no podría continuar la saga cinematográfica usando la película de Gerwig y Robbie como punto de partida. Si la empresa quisiera hacer una nueva adaptación cinematográfica basada en su icónica muñeca, tendría que ser con un reboot.
El reporte menciona que tanto los actores protagónicos como la directora y el coguionista de Barbie 2 están conformes con el salario inicial, pero no así con la compensación posterior por desempeño en taquilla. Desde Warner Bros, en tanto, Zaslav se habría mostrado inflexible ante las demandas del equipo creativo.
Gerwig y Baumbach tendrían una idea armada para Barbie 2, pero no estarían dispuestos a revelarla sin antes firmar nuevos contratos. Por lo pronto, es un misterio si esto se dará o no. Si el estudio no da el brazo a torcer y la secuela se cancela, aún quedaría una bala de plata en la figura de David Ellison. Si el empresario concreta la compra de Warner Bros con Paramount Skydance, podría repescar los derechos de Mattel para avanzar con la nueva película.
Hoy por hoy, las fichas parecen estar puestas en esperar a un cambio de conducción en WB para tratar de resolver el conflicto por Barbie 2. Muchos en Hollywood creen que Ellison será menos testarudo que Zaslav al lidiar con una propiedad intelectual que demostró ser un hit global. No olvidemos que Barbie fue uno de los fenómenos de la taquilla 2023, recaudando más de 1.447 millones de dólares a nivel mundial a partir un presupuesto de 128 millones de dólares.

articles.title: Aqua for All seeks impact-driven fund managers for catalytic capital - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Aqua for All has launched a new call for applications, inviting impact-driven fund managers with private debt, private equity, natural capital, infrastructure or other real-asset strategies to apply for catalytic funding to scale their impact across water, sanitation and closely related nexus sectors, such as energy and climate, in emerging markets.
Aqua for All will provide equity or first-loss equity, alongside technical assistance, to help de-risk investments and mobilise private sector financing, while delivering measurable environmental and social impact.
“We seek to partner with fund managers who have a strong track record of deploying capital effectively in emerging markets to advance SDG 6,” said Aqua for All.
This is the organisation’s second call for applications for fund managers, building on the first call launched one year ago in partnership with the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC) under the Catalysing Impact with Innovative Financing programme.
The programme offers investment of between EUR1 million (USS$1.15 million) and EUR5 million (US$5.7 million) into private funds to mobilise private capital participation, as well as technical assistance of up to EUR150,000 (US$170,000).
Applications are open here until August 31.

articles.title: Google unveils the latest range of Pixel 11 smartphones with deeper Gemini integration - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Google has unveiled its latest Pixel smartphone line-up which includes the Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro XL and the Pixel 11 Pro Fold.
The new range introduces even deeper Gemini Intelligence integration, the next-generation Tensor G6 processor and the Titan3 security chip.
Google has also introduced the new Pixel Watch 5 and the Pixel Tag tracker.
Pre-orders kick off today ahead of the official on-sale date of August 20.
PIXEL 11, PIXEL 11 PRO, PIXEL 11 PRO XL
One of the first things you notice with the Pixel 11 range is the thinner all-glass camera bar.
This is where you find an upgraded 48MP main sensor with 56 per cent increased light sensitivity, an enhanced 48MP telephoto supporting up to 120x zoom on Pro models.
It also offers faster Night Sight processing – up to 4.5x faster.
The new Pixel 11 line-up is built tough and has improved resistance against drops, scratches and splashes.
The Pixel Pro smartphones are available in four vibrant colours – Canyon, Olive, Fog and Obsidian.
Google Pixel 11 is available in Frost, Hibiscus, Pistachio and Obsidian.
The Google 11 Pixel Pro Fold comes in Olive and Obsidian.
The new Pixel devices are powered by the Google Tensor G6 chip with up to 16GB RAM and brighter Actua displays reaching up to 3,600 nits on the Pro models.
There is an all-new HiLight notification LED surrounding the flash system.
Users can assign up to five custom colour patterns for specific contacts and receive subtle visual updates.
Gemini Intelligence has gone to the next level and expands proactive assistance across system apps—auto-suggesting calendar events, generating Maps previews, storing loyalty numbers, and offering real-time transcriptions via Rambler.
For your photography Magic Capture takes up to multiple frames per shot to auto-select optimal HDR+ frames and offers customizable camera aesthetics directly in the viewfinder.
And you can content even easier with the Creator Suite which introduces built-in teleprompter functionality so you can nail your videos every time.
PIXEL 11 PRO FOLD
The new Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold is 10 per cent lighter and 1mm thinner than its predecessor with the thinnest bezels yet on a Pixel foldable.
The device has a glass fibre composite back, an updated hinge mechanism (3x more durable), and maintains full IP68 water resistance.
On the display side the Pro Fold features a 20 per cent brighter outer cover display and an inner flex display (up to 3,600 nits) equipped with productivity features like Bubble Anything, drag-and-drop, and split-screen support.
The onboard Tensor G6 delivers 50 per cent more GPU compute power, higher memory bandwidth, and runs Gemini Nano 3x faster while consuming 2.5x less energy.
PIXEL WATCH 5
The Pixel Watch 5 is powered by the Qualcomm Snapdragon W5 Gen 2 platform with 50 per cent more RAM and 2x more accurate GPS.
The display has scratch-resistant Gorilla Glass and has an IP68 rating.
Onboard is Google Health which can monitor blood pressure, insulin resistance trends and sleep quality metrics.
On the battery side the Google Pixel Watch 5 can run for up to 40 hours on a single charge.
GOOGLE PIXEL TAG
This Google’s version of Apple’s AirTag – a new item finder leveraging the Android Find My Device network.
The Google Pixel Tag is 28mm wide, 46mm long and weighs 11.8g.
It is powered by a single CR2032 cell battery.
There is no hole to attach it to a keyring – for this you’ll have to purchase a separate accessory.
The Google Pixel Tag will go on sale on November 11.
PRICING
The Pixel 11 is priced at $1499 (256GB), $1,699 (512GB).
The Pixel 11 Pro is $1,849 (256GB), $2,049 (512GB) and $2,399 (1TB).
The Pixel 11 Pro XL starts at $2,099 (256GB), $2,299 (512GB) and $2,649 (1TB).
The Pixel Tag is priced at $49 for a 1-pack or $169 for a 4-pack.
The Pixel Watch 5 (41mm) is $649 for the Wi-Fi model and $829 for the LTE model
The Pixel Watch 5 (45mm) is $699 for the Wi-Fi model and $879 for the LTE model

articles.title: AstroTalk turns unicorn via ESOP buyback
articles.text:
AstroTalk turns unicorn via ESOP buyback
Spiritual-tech startup AstroTalk has reached a valuation of $1 billion through an ESOP buyback involving over 100 employees.
Spiritual-tech startup AstroTalk has entered India’s unicorn club after reaching a valuation of $1 billion through an ESOP buyback, according to reports.
More than 100 employees are taking part in the buyback, which gives them an opportunity to sell some of their shares and realise part of the value created by the company, the reports said.
The transaction is said to be funded from AstroTalk’s business profits rather than through a new external funding round.
Founded in 2017 by Puneet Gupta and Anmol Jain, AstroTalk began as an online astrology consultation platform and has since then expanded into spiritual commerce. Its AstroTalk Store sells products such as gemstones, rudrakshas, bracelets, and other spiritual items.
In FY25, AstroTalk reported Rs 1,176 crore in revenue from operations, compared with Rs 651 crore the previous year. Its total income was Rs 1,214 crore, while profit before tax rose to Rs 285 crore from Rs 127 crore.
AstroTalk Store is becoming a significant part of the startup's business, generating more than Rs 140 crore in revenue in 2025, processing over 1.6 million orders.
The $1 billion valuation is a significant rise from the roughly $300 million valuation reported in 2024.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: Jetzt ausprobieren: Größte Karte des Himmels ist online
articles.text:
Über 5 Billionen Pixel: Forscher veröffentlichen die bislang größte Karte des Universums
Nach 13 Jahren Arbeit: Ein Forschungsteam hat die bisher größte zweidimensionale Karte des Universums veröffentlicht. Auf einer Webseite ist ein Viewer für jedermann zugänglich. Die Karte namens DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys soll nicht nur Wissenschaftler:innen, sondern auch interessierten Laien als Grundlage eigener Forschungen dienen.
Mit einer Skala oder der Computermaus kann man rein- oder rauszoomen. Über ein Suchfeld lassen sich namentlich bekannte Objekte direkt ansteuern. Die Auflösung der Karte beträgt 5,6 Billionen Pixel.
Karte bildet drei Viertel des Himmels ab
Bei der Karte handelt es sich um eine Projektion des Nachthimmels von der Erde aus gesehen. Der Nordpol markiert dabei den oberen Teil des Bildes, der Südpol den unteren.
DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys bildet rund drei Viertel des Himmels ab. Das nicht kartografierte Viertel liegt hauptsächlich in der Nähe der Ebene der Milchstraße, also des Teils einer Galaxie, auf dem der größte Teil ihrer Masse liegt.
Sterne und Staub, die sich dort ballen, würden die Sicht auf das extragalaktische Universum versperren und fehlen deshalb, heißt es in den FAQ zu der Karte.
Fast vier Milliarden Himmelsobjekte – nur die Planeten fehlen
Rund vier Milliarden Objekte sind auf der Karte zu sehen. Darunter sind Sterne, Asteroiden, ganze Galaxien und schwarze Löcher. Eine Gruppe von vertrauten Himmelskörpern fehlt allerdings auf der Karte: die Planeten unseres Sonnensystems.
Jupiter und Co. sind schlicht zu hell für die sensiblen Kameras, die zum Einsatz kamen. Ihr Licht würde den Blick auf blassere, weiter entfernte Galaxien überdecken. Deshalb haben die Teleskope laut den FAQ Teile des Himmels bewusst in den Momenten erfasst, in denen die Planeten gerade woanders auf ihrer Umlaufbahn unterwegs waren.
160 Forschende und 263 407 Teleskopbeobachtungen
Über 160 Forschende waren laut einer Pressemitteilung des beteiligten NOIRLab bei der Sammlung der Daten für die Karte aktiv. 20 Wissenschaftler:innen erstellten schließlich die finale Version.
Das Team griff dabei auf 263 407 Teleskopbeobachtungen zurück. Die wurden im Rahmen von drei Himmelsdurchmusterungen erstellt: dem Dark Energy Survey des Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory, dem Mayall z-band Legacy Survey vom Kitt Peak National Observatory und dem Beijing-Arizona Sky Survey vom Steward Observatory. Das erste Observatorium liegt in der chilenischen Atacama-Wüste, die beiden anderen im US-Bundesstaat Arizona.
Über 2000 Nächte in elf Jahren
Die Aufnahmen fanden während 2285 Nächten statt. Die Beobachtungen liefen über elf Jahre, von 2013 bis 2024. Ein Jahr dauerte es, den Programmcode zu entwickeln, der die Daten auswertete.
Ein Supercomputer im Lawrence Berkeley National Lab brauchte acht Wochen, um die 200 Terabyte an angefallenen Rohdaten zu verarbeiten.
Die zweidimensionale Karte dient als Vorbereitung für die größte jemals erstellte 3D-Karte des Universums. Die entsteht gerade durch Beobachtungen des Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instruments (DESI).

articles.title: Éclipse solaire ce 12 août 2026 : suivez le spectacle minute par minute (en direct)
articles.text:
Ce mercredi 12 août, la Lune passe devant le Soleil et offre une éclipse visible depuis la France. Suivez le phénomène en direct sur Numerama, de ses premières phases jusqu’à son point culminant.
 
Le grand jour est enfin arrivé : ce mercredi 12 août 2026, l’éclipse de Soleil tant attendue se produit. La Lune va s’interposer entre notre étoile et la Terre, ce qui amène le satellite à projeter son ombre à la surface de notre planète. C’est un spectacle à voir : le phénomène, qui est plutôt rare, est clairement l’évènement astronomique de l’année.
En France métropolitaine, le spectacle est partiellement visible, le Soleil étant masqué à plus de 90 %, et même 99,5 % dans le Sud-Ouest. Afin de voir la totalité de l’éclipse dans les meilleures conditions, il faut avoir fait le voyage en Espagne ou en Islande, deux pays qui sont traversés par la bande de totalité. L’éclipse sera alors totale.
Une autre option, plus accessible, est de regarder l’éclipse solaire en ligne et en direct. Ce n’est pas aussi marquant qu’en vrai, mais c’est une solution de repli qui se défend. Et justement, Numerama vous fait vivre aujourd’hui cette éclipse de Soleil en direct. Suivez avec nous ce moment exceptionnel, étape par étape.
    
        
    
    
    
        
    
    
        
Bonjour et bienvenue dans ce direct sur Numerama, consacré à l’éclipse solaire du 12 août 2026 !
 
     
 
    
    
        
L’évènement, bien sûr, est très attendu. À tel point que l’Agence spatiale européenne (ESA) a sorti en mai un trailer qui donne l’impression d’annoncer un film épique !
 
     
 
    
    
        
Selon les derniers bulletins météo du jour, les prévisions sont excellentes pour l’observation de l’éclipse. Des passages nuageux sont peut-être à redouter par endroits, mais le ciel devrait être globalement dégagé ce soir.
Si c’est le cas, il ne vous restera plus qu’à rouspéter contre les cumulus qui oseront vous barrer la vue.
 
     
 
    
    
        
Attention, n’utilisez pas n’importe quelle lunette d’éclipse. Une paire fiable doit comporter deux mentions très précises sur la monture :
À cela s’ajoutent deux autres recommandations additionnelles, pour être parfaitement dans les clous
- l’identité et les coordonnées du fabricant ou de l’importateur, ainsi qu’un moyen de traçabilité, comme un numéro de lot.
- des instructions d’utilisation en français.
C’est important, parce que l’on a pu constater que des lunettes qui ne respectent pas les normes de sécurité sont disponibles à la vente.
 
     
 
    
    
        
 
     
 
    
    
        
Cette carte, fournie par l’Agence spatiale européenne, renseigne les zones de l’hémisphère nord où l’éclipse sera visible. 
Dans toute la partie orangée, l’éclipse sera partielle, avec un degré d’occultation variable. En revanche, dans la bande étroite, plus au centre, l’éclipse sera totale.
 
     
 
    
    
        
Au fait, vous avez déjà vu une éclipse solaire depuis l’espace ? Non ? Hé bien, maintenant, oui.
Cette image est très réelle : elle a été prise par l’équipage d’Artémis II début avril 2026, quand leur vaisseau Orion effectuait le tour de la Lune. 
Très rares sont les humains à avoir pu profiter d’une telle vue.
 
     
 
    
    
        
Puisque l’on a encore un peu de temps avant l’heure H, on vous invite à visionner cette vidéo qui explique les raisons pour lesquelles cette éclipse du 12 août n’est pas du tout anodine.
 
     
 
    
    
        
Voici les degrés d’occultation pour les principales villes en France métropolitaine, selon l’Association Française d’Astronomie.
| Ville | Début | Maximum | Fin | Obscuration | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paris | 19h22 | 20h17 | 21h09* | 92,2 % | 
| Marseille | 19h31 | 20h25 | 21h15* | 96,3 % | 
| Lyon | 19h27 | 20h21 | 21h11* | 93,8 % | 
| Toulouse | 19h31 | 20h26 | 21h17* | 97,8 % | 
| Nice | 19h31 | 20h24 | 21h14* | 95,1 % | 
| Nantes | 19h24 | 20h20 | 21h13 | 96 % | 
| Montpellier | 19h31 | 20h25 | 21h15* | 96 % | 
| Strasbourg | 19h23 | 20h16 | 21h07* | 89,9 % | 
| Bordeaux | 19h29 | 20h25 | 21h17* | 97,6 % | 
| Lille | 19h19 | 20h14 | 21h06 | 90,4 % | 
| Brest | 19h22 | 20h19 | 21h13 | 96,5 % | 
| Lorient | 19h23 | 20h20 | 21h13 | 96 % | 
| La Rochelle | 19h26 | 20h22 | 21h15* | 96,8 % | 
| Biarritz | 19h31 | 20h26 | 21h18* | 99,5 % | 
 
     
 
    
    
        
Plus on descend vers le sud-ouest, plus l’occultation du Soleil sera importante.
 
     
 
    
    
        
On parle beaucoup d’éclipse, mais encore faudrait-il définir ce dont il s’agit. C’est un alignement particulier entre 3 corps : le Soleil, la Terre et la Lune. On en trouve deux types : les éclipses solaires et des éclipses lunaires. 
On distingue quatre types d’éclipses solaires :
- L’éclipse totale : la totalité du disque du Soleil est masquée par la Lune. On peut voir la couronne solaire, soit la partie la plus externe de l’atmosphère de l’étoile.
- L’éclipse partielle : la Lune ne masque qu’une partie de l’étoile.
- L’éclipse annulaire : la Lune étant plus éloignée de la Terre, elle ne bloque pas totalement le Soleil. On peut observer un anneau brillant entourant la Lune.
- L’éclipse hybride : un état intermédiaire entre une éclipse annulaire et totale.
 
     
 
    
    
        
Pour l’éclipse du 12 août, la règle est de regarder vers l’ouest tout en s’assurant d’avoir un horizon bien dégagé.
Il existe plusieurs ressources en ligne qui peuvent vous aider. On vous en cite trois : 
 
     
 
    
    
        
 
     
 
    
    
        
Techniquement, un masque de soudure peut le faire, à condition que son indice de protection se situe au moins à 12 ou 14. Le plus sûr de viser un seuil à 14 (ou plus), qui soit intact, avec une référence lisible. 
Un doute ? Ne vous en servez pas, car cela reste un matériel plutôt pour les pros.
De toute façon, le port de verres de soudeur en pleine rue va vous donner un drôle d’air.
 
     
 
    
    
        
Pas besoin cependant de recourir à un masque de soudure. Il existe une première astuce, qui mobilise un écumoire.
 
     
 
    
    
        
L’autre option ? L’astuce de la boîte à chaussures.
 
     
 
    
    
        
C’est un grand NON. Mettre des lunettes de soleil pour regarder une éclipse c’est extrêmement dangereux.
Idem sans lunettes, d’ailleurs. C’est encore pire.
 
     
 
    
    
        
Là encore, ce n’est pas recommandé de vous en servir. Leur pouvoir filtrant a pu s’estomper avec le temps et, par ailleurs, les conditions de rangement de votre ancienne paire n’ont peut-être pas été idéales. Du coup, le film UV a peut être été esquinté.
 
     
 
    
    
        
Vous avez des lunettes d’éclipse répondant aux meilleures normes. Si vous le désirez, vous pouvez aussi les vérifier directement.
Bien sûr, tout cela s’entend en manipulant avec d’infinies précautions vos lunettes pour les abimer. Et, une fois les tests effectués, il faut les ranger très soigneusement, jusqu’au moment de l’observation.
 
     
 
    
    
        
Trois tests progressifs existent pour vérifier la qualité de ses lunettes en sécurité (en manipulant avec grand soin la paire pour ne surtout pas l’abîmer) :
Le test en intérieur : mettez la paire chez vous. Vous ne devez absolument rien voir. À la limite, vous distinguerez la lueur très faible d’une ampoule très intense, ou du flash du smartphone, mais c’est tout. Si vous arrivez à distinguer les meubles autour de vous à cette étape, c’est poubelle.
Le test en extérieur : allez dehors en plein jour et regardez autour de vous (sans lever la tête vers le ciel et, surtout, le Soleil). Là encore, c’est le noir complet. Vous apercevrez peut-être un très léger reflet du Soleil sur une carrosserie ou une surface réfléchissante, mais rien de plus.
L’ultime vérification : les lunettes ont passé les deux premières étapes ? Jetez un très rapide coup d’œil au Soleil avec la monture bien calée sur le nez. Vous devez voir un disque rond aux contours parfaitement nets.
 
     
 
    
    
        
La prochaine fois que cela adviendra en France métropolitaine, nous serons le 3 septembre 2081. Autant dire que ce n’est pas demain la veille.
Et la dernière fois ? C’était le 11 août 1999.
 
     
 
    
    
        
Puisque l’on parle du CNES, sachez que l’agence spatiale française a eu la bonne idée de constituer une petite playlist sur Spotify avec des titres en lien avec notre astre. Par exemple :
Sunny de Boney M, Black Hole Sun de Soundgarden, Au Soleil de Jennifer, Here Comes the Sun de Nina Simone et, bien sûr, Total Eclipse of the Heart de Bonnie Tyler.
Forcément.
 
     
 
    
    
        
Le SE-OP (Observatoire de Paris) propose un site qui cartographie 6 800 ans d’éclipses, de -4700 à 2100.
La prévision au-delà de 2100 est limitée par les irrégularités de la rotation terrestre, qui déplacent finement la trajectoire au sol des éclipses.
Pour remonter jusqu’à l’Antiquité, les modèles s’appuient sur des archives historiques d’éclipses croisées avec des éphémérides et des mesures d’horloges atomiques.
 
     
 
    
    
        
On approche de la dernière ligne droite ! Voici un rappel des horaires
| Phase | Horaire (temps légal français, UTC+2) | 
|---|---|
| Début de l’éclipse générale | 17h34 | 
| Début de l’éclipse totale | 18h58 | 
| Début de l’éclipse centrale | 19h | 
| Maximum de l’éclipse | 19h46 (le moment qu’il ne faut pas louper !) | 
| Fin de l’éclipse centrale | 20h32 | 
| Fin de l’éclipse totale | 20h34 | 
| Fin de l’éclipse générale | 21h57 | 
 
     
 
    
    
        
Vous pouvez suivre l’évènement à distance avec ce premier flux en direct.
 
     
 
    
    
        
Un autre direct, de l’Agence spatiale européenne, qui débutera à 19h30.

articles.title: Mindgard Raises $30 Million to Protect AI Systems
articles.text:
AI security startup Mindgard today announced raising $30 million in a Series A funding round that brings the total raised by the company close to $42 million.
The investment round was led by Album VC, with additional support from Karma Ventures and previous investors .406 Ventures, Atlantic Bridge, IQ Capital, and Lakestar.
Founded in 2022, spun out of Lancaster University, and headquartered in London and Boston, Mindgard has built an automated AI security and red-teaming platform to help organizations identify and respond to AI risks.
According to the company, its platform can capture and exploit the psycho-technical attack surface within AI agents, models, and applications.
Mindgard acts as a red-teamer to identify exploits, assess risk, and defend AI systems. It maps the entire attack surface, continuously analyzes it, and delivers runtime protection to stop attacks dead in their tracks.
The solution has already uncovered over 150 vulnerabilities across popular AI products, including a zero-day code execution flaw in Cursor IDE, and security defects in Google Antigravity and ChatGPT.
Mindgard will use the fresh funding to scale its product, engineering, sales, and marketing teams. The investment will help accelerate deployments across financial services, digital services, gaming, healthcare, pharmaceutical, and semiconductor sectors.
“AI is creating an entirely new attack surface and organizations need a fundamentally different approach to securing it,” said Mindgard CEO James Brear.
“We don’t just automate attacks. We operationalize expertise, turning the knowledge of leading AI security researchers and offensive security practitioners into the capabilities every enterprise needs to secure their AI,” Brear added.

articles.title: Nigeria’s identity law raises questions over digital signatures
articles.text:
Nigeria’s new identity law could complicate the passage of a long-awaited digital economy bill, with both frameworks covering digital identity and electronic signatures and potentially creating overlapping rules for businesses and government agencies.
Under the NIMC Act 2026, which replaced the 2007 Act, the National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) is now Nigeria’s Root Certification Authority (Root CA). The designation puts NIMC at the centre of Nigeria’s digital trust infrastructure, with responsibility for issuing root digital certificates, verifying electronic identities and overseeing the trust framework for digital signatures linked to the National Identification Number (NIN).
A digital signature is a mathematical method for verifying that a digital document, email or message is authentic, has not been altered and was signed by the person claiming to have signed it.
The National Digital Economy and E-Governance Bill, however, focuses on the legal validity of electronic signatures. It explains when an electronic signature can satisfy a legal signature requirement and establishes standards for digital signatures, including identity verification, sole control by the signer, data integrity, and the ability to detect subsequent changes.
The NIMC Act makes NIMC the Root Certification Authority, while the E-Governance Bill empowers the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA), the country’s tech regulator, to regulate and accredit electronic signature Certification Authorities, creating a potential overlap in their mandates.
Both laws seek to establish the foundation for digital signatures, identity verification, and paperless government services, but their overlapping mandates could create uncertainty over who ultimately controls key parts of Nigeria’s digital trust infrastructure.
“The Act is operational at the moment; it has been passed by the President, and that is the law we have now,” a NIMC spokesperson told TechCabal via text on Wednesday. “The other one, or any other bill coming up, the National Assembly will have to take a closer look and do the needful.”
Without clear alignment between the NIMC Act and the Digital Economy Bill, government agencies, regulators, banks, and technology companies may have to comply with overlapping rules, slowing the rollout of secure digital services as they await clearer guidance, according to policy experts.
“Ideally, this should have been spotted by the legal drafting unit at the National Assembly, but with what happened with the tax bill, I’m not surprised,” said Adeboye Adegoke, a digital rights and policy expert. “Bills are supposed to be reviewed to avoid clashes with existing laws. It’s not normal for new laws to conflict or duplicate provisions in existing laws without first amending the existing one.”
The Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy did not respond to requests for comments.
NIMC as Nigeria’s digital trust infrastructure
One of the most significant changes introduced by the NIMC Act 2026 is the commission’s formal designation as Nigeria’s Root Certification Authority (RCA) and Issuing Authority for the National Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) and Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI).
The RCA is one of the most critical components of any country’s digital infrastructure.
In a Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), a system that helps people and organisations verify identities and secure digital communications, the RCA sits at the top of a chain of trust used to verify digital identities. It rarely interacts directly with citizens. Instead, it authorises intermediate certification authorities, which then issue digital certificates used by government agencies, banks, businesses and individuals.
Whenever a digital signature is verified, systems trace that signature back through this chain until they reach the RCA. If the root authority is trusted, the entire transaction is considered authentic.
Rather than merely recognising electronic signatures, the NIMC Act establishes the technical and legal architecture that allows them to function. Per Section 7(k), NIMC is responsible for validating the cryptographic certificates that underpin digital signatures, secure online transactions, digital certificates, and identity verification across government and the private sector.
The role makes NIMC the national “trust anchor” for Nigeria’s digital economy. Every authorised government agency, financial institution, or private organisation issuing trusted digital certificates would ultimately derive its authority from NIMC’s root cryptographic keys.
In practice, this means NIMC is no longer only an identity management agency but also the institution responsible for securing the country’s digital authentication infrastructure.
Significant overlap with the Digital Economy Bill
The Digital Economy and E-Governance Bill already contains detailed provisions governing electronic signatures and digital government services.
Section 16(1) requires digital signatures used in government and commercial transactions to be linked directly to an individual’s National Identification Number (NIN), with identity verification conducted through secure APIs connected to NIMC’s identity database.
The bill also gives qualifying electronic signatures the same legal validity as handwritten signatures, provided they are uniquely linked to the signer, remain under the user’s sole control, and can be detected as subsequent alterations.
“In any proceedings involving a digital signature, it shall be presumed, unless evidence to the contrary is adduced, that– (a) the digital signature is the signature of the person to whom it correlates; and (b) the digital signature was axed by that person with the intention of signing or approving the electronic record,” the bill stated in section 18.
Sections 44, 45 and 46 seek to make Nigerian public administration paperless by requiring ministries, departments, and agencies to issue, receive, and store official records electronically while relying on digital signatures for authentication.
Many of these objectives are now reinforced—or arguably pre-empted—by the new NIMC Act.
By establishing the national Public Key Infrastructure, reaffirming the NIN as the country’s foundational identity under the “One Person, One Identity” framework, and empowering NIMC to build secure data-sharing systems across public institutions, the Act already creates much of the infrastructure needed for the Digital Economy Bill to function.
A bill years in the making
The National Digital Economy and E-Governance Bill has undergone an extensive legislative process.
The proposal was first introduced in July 2024 by Adedeji Dhikrullahi Olajide, Chairman of the House Committee on Digital and Information Technology.
Following consultations with technology companies, civil society organisations and government agencies, lawmakers have revised the bill to align with broader digital infrastructure projects, including Nigeria’s nationwide fibre rollout, according to the Ministry of Communication, Innovation, and Digital Economy.
At a joint National Assembly public hearing on November 10, 2025, Minister of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy Bosun Tijani said the legislation had completed major stakeholder reviews and was expected to proceed through harmonisation before being transmitted to President Bola Tinubu for assent.
By May 2026, the bill had been approved by the House of Representatives and was awaiting consideration by the Senate.
However, the enactment of the NIMC Act before the bill’s final passage has introduced new legal considerations that lawmakers may need to resolve.
“This is now law, so it goes ahead of the Digital Economy bill — which will now need to be revised,” ‘Gbenga Sesan, executive director, Paradigm Initiative, a pan-African social enterprise that connects underserved people-groups with ICT-enabled opportunities, told TechCabal. “NIMC is with another Ministry, so it’s clear they were not exchanging notes.”
Lessons from other African countries
Nigeria’s evolving framework also differs from digital signature governance models adopted elsewhere on the continent.
In Kenya, the Communications Authority licences electronic certification providers, while the ICT Authority operates the government’s certification infrastructure. South Africa relies on an Accreditation Authority under its Department of Communications and Digital Technologies to certify advanced electronic signatures.
Egypt assigns similar responsibilities to the Information Technology Industry Development Agency (ITIDA), which licences trusted certification providers while operating the government’s certification authority.
All three countries rely on Public Key Infrastructure, but oversight rests with specialised technology regulators rather than national identity agencies.
Nigeria’s decision to position NIMC as both the national identity authority and Root Certification Authority creates a more centralised governance model, one that could simplify implementation but also increase the importance of ensuring legal clarity across overlapping digital economy laws.
Until those overlaps are addressed, the country’s flagship Digital Economy Bill may face another round of legislative scrutiny before becoming law.

articles.title: Una cosechadora en Guadalajara, un cable en Almería, unas obras en Huesca: España tiene que repensar su vida en verano para evitar incendios
articles.text:
El jueves 16 de julio de 2026, en La Mierla, al norte de la provincia de Guadalajara fue "una cosechadora agrícola". En Burgohondo, al sur de Ávila, fue "una imprudencia grave por el empleo de maquinaria pesada". En Los Gallardos, al norte de Almería, fue un cable olvidado y las Peñas de Riglos, en la hoya de Huesca, las sospechas apuntan a una campa de unas obras en la A-132.
Faltan datos oficiales y meses de investigaciones, pero algo está claro algo no funciona en la normativa. España es ahora mismo el meme del perro que, en mitad de una cafetería en llamas, dice "it's fine" y sigue a lo suyo. Pero no podemos seguir así.
Una normativa con agujeros. Aunque no suele hablarse de esto, muchas de estas cosas están "prohibidas" en España. Desde el Real Decreto-ley 15/2022, la Ley de Montes prohíbe usar maquinaria "cuyo funcionamiento genere deflagración, chispas o descargas eléctricas" cuando AEMET prevé riesgo muy alto o extremo, y el RD 716/2025 extendió esa prohibición a una franja de 400 metros alrededor del monte, salvo autorización expresa.
El problema real es que "prohibir" quizás sea un término excesivo para un sistema de excepciones, declaraciones responsables y ventanas horarias. En La Mierla, hasta donde sabemos, se podía cosechar; con algunas medidas de seguridad, pero se podía.
La maraña de regulaciones es muy densa... Castilla-La Mancha y Extremadura suspenden los trabajos de 14:00 a 17:00 y Galicia lo hace de 12:00 a 18:00. Castilla y León permite cosechar con matachispas "salvo que la temperatura sea superior a 30 ºC y la velocidad del viento supere los 30 km/h". Las dos cosas a la vez.
Y así podríamos seguir comunidad a comunidad porque no existe una normativa nacional que regule este tipo de cosas. De hecho, a la obra pública se le aplica el mismo tipo de regulación que a los agricultores.
...y poco efectiva. Al menos, cuando el verano se desborda. Es decir, en veranos como este. El avance del MITECO a 2 de agosto contaba 144.844,80 hectáreas quemadas. Eso es el 0,507 % de la superficie forestal nacional. Casi dos veces y media por encima del 0,207 % de la media de los últimos 10 años. Pero los datos del sistema europeo EFFIS, que usa imágenes satelitales y actualiza más rápido, hablaba de a 222.783 hectáreas a 5 de agosto, el 44,5 % de todo lo quemado en la Unión Europea.
Si la situación sigue así (y seguirá), nuestra regulación está claramente obsoleta.
Una bomba de relojería. Sobre todo porque investigaciones como la de la UPNA, la Universidad de Zaragoza y Fundación Mapfre señalan que, aunque este tipo de maquinaria no es la primera causa de incendios forestales, sí que tienen la capacidad de provocar incendios muy destructivos porque coincide (en el tiempo y en el espacio) con las peores condiciones de propagación.
¿Y qué hacer? Si miramos al exterior la respuesta parece clara: ser más restrictivos. Y sí, parece difícil congeniar la necesidad de regular más con la idea de que el campo está hiperregulado, pero es así: históricamente, las regulaciones han surgido para solucionar problemas que el mal uso, la mala fe y las imprudencias iban generando.
Y no es tan difícil, En Portugal, por ejemplo, tras años de situaciones críticas no veta ya unas pocas horas; desplaza toda la actividad a la noche. En Oregon hacen algo similar en niveles medios, pero prohibi directamente todo cuando el riesgo es alto.
No es tan raro como parece. Desde hace años, en España la normativa para el trabajo al aire libre va por ese camino y cambia automáticamente en cuanto AEMET modifica las alertas.
La pregunta es cuánto vamos a tardar en tomarnos en serio

articles.title: Code that passes every test can still break the next AI agent that touches it
articles.text:
Code that passes every test can still break the next AI agent that touches it
Originally designed to make software predictable for humans, Google Go is now positioning itself as a language tailored for machine authors. On Tuesday, August 11, Google made its case on the Google Developers Blog, pointing to Go’s small language surface, static type system, and integrated development tools as essential guardrails that help AI coding agents catch and fix their own mistakes.
With coding agents producing code far faster than developers can review it, the engineering challenge is shifting to checking and maintaining it.
Fewer choices, fewer mistakes
What some developers like about Go, others find frustrating. The language is relatively small, which deliberately limits syntax, so its standard gofmt tool applies the same formatting everywhere. For an AI agent, it reduces the number of possible patterns it can generate and makes the expected output easier to identify.
For that reason, Go’s compiler immediately rejects nonexistent methods, incorrect types, and other structural mistakes that might remain hidden until runtime in a dynamically typed language. But the compiler cannot tell whether the agent misunderstood the assignment, applied the wrong business rule or exposed information to the wrong user, so human oversight is still needed.
The compiler cannot tell whether the agent misunderstood the assignment, applied the wrong business rule or exposed information to the wrong user, so human oversight is still needed.
Toolchain as agent guardrail
An agent working in Go can format a change with gofmt, run the test suite, probe unexpected inputs with native fuzzing and use govulncheck to find calls to vulnerable functions without first figuring out which third-party tools a project has adopted. If it downloads a module, Go’s checksum database can flag a copy that no longer matches the recorded version.
The standard library may also reduce a risk specific to machine-generated code. Coding models sometimes recommend obsolete, abandoned, or nonexistent packages based on patterns in their training data, but none of these protections eliminate software supply chain risk. Vulnerability scanning is limited by what has been discovered and entered into the database.
The gopls language server can now send compiler errors and code analysis directly to AI tools through an MCP server, while the rebuilt go fix in Go 1.26 can update older code using predefined transformations instead of asking a model to rewrite it from scratch.
These tools effectively become part of the agent harness. The model proposes a change, and automated tools check whether it conforms to the language and project.
Coding models sometimes recommend obsolete, abandoned, or nonexistent packages based on patterns in their training data.
Maintainability after the merge
A June 2026 study, “Is Agent Code Less Maintainable Than Human Code?“, attempted to measure that downstream effect. The researchers created CodeThread, a framework in which coding agents completed follow-up tasks on either human-written or agent-written implementations of an earlier task.
Across four coding agents and four benchmarks, agents were less successful when building on code previously written by an agent. The difference in task-resolution rates reached 13.1% in some comparisons, even though both the human and agent implementations had initially passed the tests. The researchers found subtler variations in input validation, error handling, and implementation behavior.
Code review research points to a similar problem. A separate study of 278,790 inline review conversations across 300 open source projects found that human reviewers went through 11.8% more review rounds when reviewing agent-written code than human-written code.
AI review suggestions were adopted 16.6% of the time, compared with 56.5% for suggestions from human reviewers. When AI suggestions were accepted, they produced larger increases in code size and complexity. Human reviewers were more likely to raise questions about testing, understanding, and knowledge transfer.
None of the studies gave agents the same task in Go, Python, JavaScript and Rust, so they cannot show that Go produces more maintainable code. What they do show is that code can pass its original tests and still trip up the next agent, leaving human developers to handle most of the changes that follow.
None of the studies gave agents the same task in Go, Python, JavaScript and Rust, so they cannot show that Go produces more maintainable code.
Boring wins when speed scales
Agents don’t mind the repetitive work that human developers may find tedious. In Go, the compiler flags an incorrect type, the formatter keeps every file consistent, and the test runner shows whether a change works before the code reaches a reviewer.
Go is not the only language with those guardrails, but the restrictions that once made it seem boring look different when machines can produce more code than people have time to read.

articles.title: A years-long investigation just unmasked a major torrent pirate, the how remains unclear
articles.text:
What just happened? Kyoto Prefectural Police have arrested a man accused of uploading copyrighted TV programs to the torrent site Nyaa, following an investigation that began several years ago. The case has drawn attention because the investigation does not appear to have relied on the usual method of joining BitTorrent swarms and identifying users who are sharing files. Instead, CODA, a Japanese anti-piracy organization, said it examined how information moves between torrent index sites and trackers.
Police arrested Masakazu Ono, 56, of Sagamihara in Kanagawa Prefecture. He is accused of acting as an initial seeder, meaning he was allegedly the first person to make complete files available for others to download. One of the files tied to the case was reportedly Midnight Taxi, a 2026 drama produced by NHK and WOWOW.
Authorities said Ono had uploaded nearly 1,000 NHK recordings during the investigation.
CODA began looking into Nyaa uploaders in 2021 through its Cross-Border Enforcement Project. The group worked with the Japan Hacker Association, known as JHA, before Kyoto police joined the case in 2024. Three alleged secondary uploaders connected to "reach sites" were charged in 2025. Those sites appear to be link aggregators that direct users to torrent files.
The details of how investigators identified Ono have not been made public. CODA said it "analyzed how data moves through torrent sites, such as index sites and tracker sites." That leaves open several possibilities.
Torrent index sites and trackers serve different roles. An index site is the public-facing page where users find torrent files. A tracker works in the background. BitTorrent software connects to it to find other users involved with the same file.
Trackers can show which users are active in a torrent at a given time. They may indicate whether a user has a complete copy of a file or is still downloading it. If investigators followed newly posted torrents over a long period, they may have been able to identify an IP address that repeatedly appeared as the first source with a complete copy.
That would fit the length of the investigation. A single upload may not provide much evidence, but a pattern across hundreds of files could help connect an account or network address to the original source of the material.
JHA's involvement is also significant. Its founder, Takayuki Sugiura, is known for decrypting the Winny peer-to-peer protocol in 2004 to identify original uploaders. Nyaa and Winny are different systems, but both involve tracing the source of files that spread across decentralized networks.
There are other ways investigators could have connected activity to Ono. He may have used Nyaa without a VPN while logged into an account. Data from website cookies or content-delivery-network logs could also have been matched with Nyaa activity and tracker records. CODA has not said whether any of those methods were used.
The more common approach in piracy investigations is to run a tracker honeypot or enter a torrent swarm and record the IP addresses of people sharing a file. That may not have been the approach in this case. Nyaa uses a small group of established trackers, and CODA's description points more toward analysis of the site's infrastructure than direct participation in a swarm.
Japanese law also limits broad monitoring of internet traffic. Methods such as deep packet inspection or large-scale traffic-volume monitoring would likely face legal concerns before authorities had identified a suspect.

articles.title: Vivo Easy Lite muda de nome e ganha nova forma de pagamento • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Vivo Easy Lite muda de nome e ganha nova forma de pagamento
Preços começam em R$ 35 por mês, com 20 GB de internet móvel.
Se você assina algum plano Vivo Easy Lite, talvez já tenha notado que, desde a semana passada, a modalidade passou a se chamar simplesmente Vivo Lite. A mudança de nomenclatura é acompanhada da adição de uma nova forma de pagamento: o Pix.
Os efeitos da alteração já aparecem no site da operadora: as páginas do Vivo Easy Lite foram modificadas para exibir apenas o nome Vivo Lite. A Vivo não explicou o motivo da mudança de nome, mas esclareceu ao Tecnoblog que os benefícios oferecidos nos planos foram mantidos.
Em termos práticos, a única novidade é mesmo a adição do Pix como forma de pagamento. Até então, os planos Lite aceitavam apenas pagamento via cartão de crédito.
O site da operadora destaca três opções de planos Vivo Lite. São eles:
|  | Vivo Lite 20 GB | Vivo Lite 30 GB | Vivo Lite 40 GB | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Franquia | 20 GB por mês | 30 GB por mês | 40 GB por mês | 
| Preço anual | – | 12 x R$ 30 no cartão | 12 x R$ 40 no cartão | 
| Preço mensal | R$ 35 | R$ 45 | R$ 55 | 
| Benefício extra | 2 meses de YouTube | 2 meses de YouTube | 2 meses de YouTube | 
O pagamento anual é mais interessante porque, como a cobrança é feita em 12 vezes no cartão de crédito, na prática, o assinante desembolsa R$ 30 por mês no plano de 30 GB ou R$ 40 mensais no pacote de 40 GB.
Em todas as opções, o usuário tem acesso ilimitado ao YouTube durante dois meses, sem que o tráfego do serviço seja descontado da franquia. Ligações, SMS e 50% de desconto em ingressos do Cinemark estão entre os demais benefícios oferecidos.
Pelo menos até certo ponto, os planos Vivo Lite concorrem com os pacotes Claro Flex, que, atualmente, oferecem opções que começam em R$ 44,90 (35 GB).
Já na TIM, as alternativas mais próximas são os planos TIM Controle Fit, que partem de 12 vezes de R$ 20 para 25 GB de franquia por mês.

articles.title: MobileSyrup's first impressions of Google's Pixel 11 series
articles.text:
Google has just shown off six new products for its Made by Google event: the Pixel Watch 5, the Pixel Tag, and the Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro XL and Pixel 11 Pro Fold. Ahead of the event, I got the opportunity to go hands-on with each of these devices (except the Pixel Tag), but definitely focused a lot more on the company’s latest smartphone offerings — despite the lack of evolution from last year to this.
The Mountain View, California-based tech giant’s Pixel 11 series is another small iterative step, with the devices showing minimal updates versus the previous iterations. In fact, in some cases there were downgrades between the Pixel 10 series and the Pixel 11, and now the handsets unfortunately come with a higher price tag. Of course, with RAM shortages, most devices are more expensive this year, but it’s not a great time for it considering the lack of upgrades.
Don’t get me wrong, the Pixel 11 series isn’t an exact replica of its predecessor, as the Pro series comes with new hardware, called HiLight, replacing the old LED flash.
Hi, Light 👋
HiLight, available only on the Pro models, is the company’s replacement for the LED flash with some cool tricks up its sleeve. HiLight is an array of ambient LED lights built around the camera’s flash and offers a visual cue when you need to pick up your phone.
You can get a customized colour glow for incoming calls from your favourite contacts. Google has integrated this functionality with the Phone app and WhatsApp.
HiLight also works with Gemini, offering a visual cue whenever Gemini is listening, thinking and responding. I watched this feature in action, and it works fine, with Gemini changing colours as you speak to the phone.
HiLight is a nice touch. I always thought that it was weird that companies got rid of notification LEDs, and this is a fun, gimmicky way of bringing them back.
However, I think it’ll take me a while to get used to the big white circular LED that’s now featured on the camera bar. I was talking with my partner about it, showing him the leaks, and he thought this LED light is far better than the standard, so it’s probably just my own bias.
It’s also weird that the base Pixel 11 also has the HiLight-like LED without the actual feature. I guess there’s a case for uniformity and keeping the same look between all the Pixel 11s, but it could also mislead people into thinking the base Pixel 11 sports HiLight.
HiLight seems like a feature that some people will love, but unfortunately I’m not one of them. I’ll appreciate it for sure, especially when my phone is lying on its front and I want to speak with Gemini, but otherwise it’s definitely something I can see myself eventually forgetting about.
Pro performance?
The Pixel 11 series all include the Tensor G6, which offers an upgraded CPU that delivers up to 20 per cent more battery power efficiency, 25 per cent faster browsing and 15 per cent faster app loading.
I’d love to see the Tensor G6 outperform other devices, but Tensor has been lagging behind. I’m hoping this year things change, but only by going through the paces will I be able to see how Tensor is doing compared to the competition.
Google says that Tensor G6 should improve on-device Gemini experiences, as well as improve the Imaging Signal Processor (ISP) for better photography.
Magic Capture
Speaking of the ISP, I haven’t played with the cameras yet, but Google didn’t really do anything here in terms of specs. The 11 Pro now offers 120x Pro Zoom, which is interesting because the camera specs haven’t changed from last year, and you’re still getting 5x optical zoom. But the company is using its software to get up to this magnification.
There’s also a new feature called Magic Capture, which takes little videos with one tap. Then Magic Capture pulls out high-quality photos that have been automatically cropped and unblurred. As of right now, Magic Capture only takes pictures from the captured content, but this might change in the future.
Google also promises that Night Sight has improved due to a 50 per cent faster TPU from the Tensor G6. The Pixel 11 Pro series also offers ‘Instant Night Sight,’ which captures night photos without having to wait.
Strangely, all of the Pixel Pro devices have smaller batteries. Not by a lot, but it’s a strange move on Google’s part. However, now that the Tensor G6 offers better power efficiency, your handset’s battery might be similar to its predecessor, but it’s unlikely that it’ll be better. The base Pixel 11 has a slightly larger battery, so I’d expect better battery life on that device.
Canyon
One of my favourite things about the Pixel 11 devices is the colour options. The base Pixel 11 comes in Pistachio and Hibiscus variants that look good, but the Pixel 11 Pro’s colour variants are great.
The 11 Pro’s Canyon colour variant is essentially a pink with gold-ish accents that can change in the light. I was immediately drawn to this colour variant, and it continues my theory of 2026 being the year for pink phones. However, I was also quite impressed by the Obsidian Pixel 11 Pro that’s matte all around, including the frame. I think this device looks so sleek and is very reminiscent of the matte black iPhone 7.
I still like the design of the Pixel devices. I was hoping that they would be slimmer, especially considering the other handsets on the market. Though it’s worth noting that each of the devices is slightly slimmer and lighter, but I couldn’t tell just by holding them. In fact, I was pretty surprised by this when I was working on the spec sheets because they felt nearly the same as their predecessors.
The Pixel 11 Pro Fold’s crease seems pretty noticeable, especially coming from the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8.
In comparison to Samsung’s Z Fold 8 or Z Fold 8 Ultra, the Pixel 11 Pro’s crease can be seen from a variety of different angles. It’s nice that the 11 Pro Fold is IP68 water- and dustproof, though.
Not enough
I think the differences between the Pixel 11 and 10 series are pretty minimal. I definitely would prefer if we saw some bigger changes this year, but unfortunately that isn’t the case.
I’ve always been a big fan of Google’s devices, but lately the Pixel makers have been playing it too safe for hardware and going all in on AI. But with many of the AI features making it to other Android handsets, it makes the Pixel 11 series a hard sell for this year.
I still need to put the Pixel 11 series through its paces, but if they’re anything like the Pixel 10 series, they’ll be solid choices.
However, the devices are more expensive than we expected. The Pixel 11 starts at $1,249, the 11 Pro at $1,499, the Pro XL costs $1,799, and lastly, the 11 Pro Fold costs $2,269.
For the Pixel 11, the cost is pretty much the same as the 10, going up $20. It’s worth noting that the price disparity between the Pixel 10 and 11 looks great, but that’s because it started at 128GB of storage. This is similar to the Pixel 11 Pro and the Pixel 10 Pro, which started at 128GB and now go up to 256GB. However, there is still a pretty big price jump, such as the 10 Pro XL that cost $1,629 at launch, and now the 11 Pro XL costs $1,799.
The Pixel 11 series is now available for pre-order, and you can purchase the devices on August 20.

articles.title: Intel CEO hints at return to the memory business — says market is ripe for innovation, hints at stacking memory and CPU
articles.text:
Intel CEO hints at return to the memory business — says market is ripe for innovation, hints at stacking memory and CPU
Memory again?
Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan has revealed that new memory architectures — once thought a commodity business — are now strategically interesting and one of his pet projects, while speaking about the comeback of the American chip industry. He further noted that the memory industry is ripe for innovation, and also hinted at exploring ways to stack memory on top of a CPU.
After years of being a commodity, memory became a strategic asset in recent quarters and will likely remain one for a while, so suddenly, leading makers of 3D NAND and DRAM became highly profitable companies, something the Intel CEO is keenly aware of: "I used to be, 'do not invest in memory because it is a kind of commodity business,' but now it has become different," Tan said. […] "There is a lot of new technology coming out. So, we are kind of looking at one of my pet projects, some of the new memory architecture. I think you just saw the news: I hired my good friend, Seok-Hee Lee, who used to run SK Hynix. So, you kind of know something that I am thinking about. We are not ready to unfold it."
Tan did not reveal anything about the pet project and did not even specify whether the project is one of his personally favored strategic initiatives at Intel, or an initiative in one of the companies that he has invested in. He did mention that stacking memory on top of a CPU could make a lot of sense, though did not elaborate. Tan's remarks also follow the revelation of an Intel XBM patent that does away with the silicon interposer of HBM.
" I think CPU and memory, I think there are a lot of ways we can really do stacking together," Tan said. "And also try to find some new architecture for memory. I think in some way the memory, a lot of innovation are not there. So, there is some really good area."
Not everyone in the industry remembers, but Intel started as a memory company in 1968 and was quite a successful memory maker until the eighties, when Japanese companies took the lead, and Intel had to exit the market completely after suffering severe losses. Since then, the company has attempted either to return to the memory market with NAND and Optane, or at least to capitalize on a new type of memory with RDRAM. In all three cases, the company abandoned its memory initiatives without incurring significant losses.
Given the current profitability of 3D NAND and DRAM makers, producing memory is certainly a good business again and will remain profitable for some time. However, to re-enter it, companies like Intel would need capital to build at least one fab, R&D to develop competitive process technologies, and time. While licensing a technology — assuming that a company has capital — is an option, we strongly doubt that at this point Intel may be inclined to invest capital in memory and not in its core products and foundry businesses. Furthermore, it is unclear how investors react to such investments given the fact that the company struggles to become a strong competitor in the foundry market and has exited 3D NAND and 3DXPoint/Optane businesses after failing to achieve strategic targets.
Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.
