articles.title: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings raises $2B to bring AI to the enterprise | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Thrive Holdings has raised $2 billion in new funding at a $12 billion valuation from investors like SoftBank, D1 Capital Partners, and Altimeter Capital.
Thrive Holdings is akin to a private equity firm for AI, buying traditional businesses like accounting firms and implementing AI into their workflows. So far, Thrive has focused on accounting and information technology, but part of Wednesday’s raise will go toward expanding a new vertical in physical assets. Key to that strategy is Thrive’s close relationship with OpenAI.
The New York Times was first to report the news.
The firm is a spinout of Thrive Capital, one of OpenAI’s major investors. In December 2025, OpenAI took an ownership stake in Thrive Holdings. Part of the deal involved OpenAI sending employees to work with Thrive’s companies to accelerate AI adoption.
That hands-on model of AI implementation has become a business in its own right, and may help explain investor enthusiasm behind Thrive’s latest fundraise. OpenAI and Anthropic have both partnered with large private equity firms to launch The Deployment Company and Ode with Anthropic, respectively — billion-dollar ventures that are building teams of elite engineers who embed themselves into enterprises and implement AI solutions into workflows.
The raise comes off the back of proven success for Thrive’s companies, which has surpassed 70 businesses on Thrive Holdings’ platforms. The company has focused on two pillars to date: Current, its accounting arm with more than 50 firms and more than 2,000 professionals, and Shield, its information technology arm with around 20 companies on the platform.
Current’s self-improving tax agents, dubbed TaxAI, processed more than 7,000 tax returns at 98% accuracy, lowering tax prep times at participating firms by over 30%, according to Thrive. Meanwhile, Shield’s AI products have sped up help desk resolution times by 36x, and the platform has doubled the number of custom AI agents deployed in the last month.
Part of Wednesday’s fundraise will help Thrive launch a third platform focused on regulatory services for the built environment, described by a spokesperson as: “the work required to get physical assets approved, built, certified, and kept in operation.”
“The U.S. needs to build and modernize more critical infrastructure, but projects are often constrained by local, technical, and regulatory complexity,” Anuj Mehndiratta, a founding member of Thrive Holdings, told TechCrunch. “This applies across data centers, manufacturing, healthcare, power, water, transportation, and other physical infrastructure.”
That sort of complexity is where Thrive, well, thrives — large, fragmented, mission-critical, and operationally complex. While Mehndiratta says AI won’t replace field work, local judgement, or professional sign-off, it can help ease manual workflows like research, reporting, permit preparation, inspection documentation, and compliance tracking.
“We think AI partnered with a lot of the experts and practitioners at these businesses can really help compress [regulatory bottlenecks], keep the safety standards high, but also be able to do it with less of a burden to the actual building of that and help it do it more efficiently, lower cost and do it faster,” Kareem Zaki, a founding member of Thrive Holdings, said in a statement emailed to TechCrunch.

articles.title: MCP Goes Stateless, and Developers Ask Whether That Just Makes It an API Again
articles.text:
The MCP 2026-07-28 specification drops protocol sessions. Coverage so far has framed that as a scaling win, and it is one. But the same release adds two required HTTP headers, and those headers let a gateway route, throttle and meter agent traffic without ever opening the request body.
Earlier transports opened with an initialize and initialized exchange that established a session, tracked through an Mcp-Session-Id header. Every subsequent request had to locate the state tied to that session. Autoscaling infrastructure had to preserve sessions, deployments had to drain or migrate them, and load balancing was impractical, because a client was pinned to whichever instance held its session.
The new protocol removes the handshake, the session header, and protocol sessions from the core request path. Each request carries the protocol version, client identity, and capabilities it needs. Any request can land on any instance.
The part drawing less attention is what happens to the request itself. MCP messages are JSON-RPC over HTTP, and information about a request previously lived only inside the JSON body. A gateway had to parse that body to learn whether a request listed tools, invoked one, or read a resource.
Two headers are now mandatory on Streamable HTTP requests: Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name. A tool call arrives as Mcp-Method: tools/call and Mcp-Name: search, with the JSON-RPC payload behind it. Cloudflare's Matt Carey spells out what that buys you. A gateway, rate limiter or WAF can read those headers and act on them, per method or per tool, using the same primitives it already applies to every other API. Commenter evalstate noted the spec goes further still: tool arguments can be copied into headers for custom routing.
MCP request routing through gateway controls using the new headers (Source: Cloudflare)
Agent governance has been arriving from the other direction until now. Cloudflare's agent tracing and the AI Gateway tier of Azure API Management both sit above the protocol as a separate control layer. This release puts the metadata in the transport, where infrastructure teams already run can read it.
Elicitation breaks. Server-initiated requests used to need an open stream. They now use Multi Round-Trip Requests: the server returns input_required, the client collects the answer, and the call is retried. Approval becomes two requests instead of one held connection, which is simpler to deploy but means the wait for a human no longer sits inside a single invocation.
Authorization tightened alongside, with Dynamic Client Registration deprecated and slated for removal after summer 2027, RFC 9207 issuer identification adopted, and clients sending the canonical server URI as the RFC 8707 resource so tokens are accepted only by that audience.
Community reactions on Hacker News have been sharply divided, and the division is not about whether statelessness is an improvement. It is about what the improvement reveals.
For one camp, the release confirms the protocol should never have been stateful. As commenter drdexebtjl put it:
In retrospect, stateful MCP was clearly wrong. This essentially makes MCP just another REST API endpoint, and lets you use the same infrastructure you already have set up for REST APIs (like load balancers, API gateways, progressive rollouts, etc).
Commenter pjmlp framed it as a lesson the industry keeps relearning, recalling the same conclusion from Sun RPC: stateless servers are always better, stateful only when unavoidable. Commenter luciana1u was blunter:
we invented a stateful protocol, discovered state is hard to scale, stripped it out, and arrived at "just send a POST request." the REST crowd has been smugly waiting for this moment for 20 years.
Commenter bloppe made the structural version, describing MCP as a REST-like API, plus a spec of the kind OpenAPI already provides, plus harness-level authorization, and arguing only the third is genuinely new.
The defense did not dispute the resemblance so much as the conclusion. Commenter lexicality noted MCP is literally JSON-RPC, and that what was invented was a convention models were already trained to use. Commenter vidarh put the case most economically:
The core advantage MCP gave you was a standard that by virtue of being blessed by AI providers people had strong incentives to actually implement.
Implementers reached a similar verdict from the other direction. David Cramer, co-founder and chief product officer at Sentry, who had previously written publicly that MCP was not yet good, told Cloudflare the release cleans up the handling of auth and tools:
Agents only get useful once the plumbing stops being the whole story.
A parallel thread questioned whether agents need a protocol at all rather than shell access to ordinary CLI tools. Commenter firasd pushed back that the CLI position assumes a developer, on a laptop, with a shell open inside a coding harness, which describes a small fraction of usage against a majority reached through phone apps, web chat, and embedded widgets.
Adoption is not in dispute: Anthropic reports MCP passed 400 million monthly SDK downloads, a fourfold increase this year. Whether that adoption reaches individual servers is another question. A consultancy post on r/AI_Agents described auditing a client's server that recorded 61 tool calls in three months, 58 of them from the client's own engineers, and argued teams treat being reachable by an agent as though it meant being wanted by one. The author, who disclosed that MCP work is a significant share of their consulting revenue, drew a conclusion that lands on this release:
The money is flowing to the gateways and registries and auth layers rather than to the servers themselves.
For teams already running MCP in production, the migration is real work. Servers depending on protocol sessions, server-to-client requests, or standalone streams can run a stateless route beside the existing sessionful one, move features across, drain active sessions, and remove the legacy path during the deprecation window. The specification and updated TypeScript, Python, Go, and C# SDKs are available now.

articles.title: Vertical Integration Becoming Pervasive
articles.text:
No system can be optimized without an understanding of both the hardware and software, and to make the right architectural choice requires cooperation.
Key Takeaways:
Thirty years ago, there was a lot of interest in hardware/software co-design, including the mapping of software onto pre-defined hardware platforms. At that time, the technology was not good enough to make a significant difference. The industry went in the direction of using assemblies of pre-verified IP blocks, which were integrated together rather than a top-down design flow based on partitioning.
Much of the technology developed at that time has long been abandoned, but remnants do remain, such as virtual prototyping. Coupled with that are untimed and approximately timed SystemC models. Today, those virtual prototypes encompass many more engines, but they are still not viewed as being an adequate solution for realistic workloads encountered today.
This has extended into more areas today. “Long gone are the days of a hardware team building something then throwing it over the wall to an embedded software team,” says Steve Roddy, chief marketing officer at Quadric. “That era died more than two decades ago. In the past decade, virtual prototyping has extended to modeling of physical inputs and sensor interfaces in what is known as virtual twin modeling.”
When an application becomes stable, such as an audio processor or video encoder, customized hardware is more efficient than general-purpose processors. This led to a limited market for co-design and development tools. However, the development of hardware and software was not aligned. The software was relatively fixed, and the hardware was developed to optimize the running of that software.
Today’s systems are massive compared to those of several decades ago, designed for specific workloads as defined by software. At the same time, software iteration time is now much faster than hardware, making co-design a catch-up game for hardware. New tools are being developed to improve this situation. This may sound like déjà vu for industry veterans, because the tide has again turned toward custom ASICs. But this one has its own special twist.
“Historically, we have constructed abstraction layers between different parts of the software stack and different parts of the hardware stack to manage complexity for developers, with the ultimate goal of development efficiency and reliability,” says Arvind Srinivasan, design verification solutions engineer at Normal Computing. “What we have seen change is the need to squeeze optimization out of every part of the tool chain, particularly for highly performance-sensitive workloads like AI.”
A significant overlap between the needs of large AI processors and small embedded controllers is the ability to quickly and effectively create custom processors. “IP companies are focusing on making sure they are designing hardware around customer workloads and application focus,” says Sean Murphy, senior director of product at MIPS/GlobalFoundries. “This is how architectures like RISC-V are finding their differentiation in these application spaces.”
While significant progress has been made in the way that individual processors are designed, tools have more problems addressing system-level issues. “It’s all about the application or workload that you are trying to execute and understanding aspects of that — how that application affects the architecture,” says Andy Meier, principal product marketing manager for Siemens EDA. “Architecture is overloaded in that it includes both the macro-level hardware architecture, and the micro-architecture, really understanding the instructions and how certain instructions might help. In addition, it includes the software architecture, and it’s really understanding that software workload, that application, and what it is trying to accomplish.”
We remain a long way from that ultimate goal of designing hardware and software together. “We still have software teams working in their own way with their own tools, and hardware teams working with their own,” says Sam Grove, head of software and tools at MIPS/GlobalFoundries. “There is a fundamental divide that exists, and it needs to change. How do you bring the software teams and hardware teams closer together and make sure that their design flows translate to and from each other?”
Makimoto’s Wave
Back in the 1990s, Tsugio Makimoto, then CTO at Sony, made an observation about how the industry appeared to go in waves between specialize and generalize. Since then, the market has become a lot more fragmented, but that wave continues to happen in an asynchronous manner between sectors. A more concerted move started with new requirements for edge processors that suddenly demanded greater processing power while remaining within power envelopes associated with batteries. This focus on power has spread to data centers, where thermal has become a major concern, but here it is about power densities restricting what is possible in AI.
“Twenty-five years ago, there was an ASIC for every little thing,” says Siemens’ Meier. “Then we moved to the era of general-purpose processors and the industry collapsed down to just a few architectures. Today, we are seeing a lot of purpose-driven specific silicon being developed. From a shift-left perspective, instead of things being serial in a typical silicon lifecycle, those phases are overlapping — and they’re overlapping more.”
Data centers used to be packed with x86 processors. Similarly, mobile phones all used Arm processors. Then AI demanded a different type of compute, and the data centers became packed with GPUs. “There’s conventional hardware, such as GPUs, and there’s the question of whether GPUs are the end of the story,” says Patrick Coles, chief scientist at Normal Computing. “There’s increasing evidence that they aren’t, and the world is going to be full of ASICs. It’s going to be heterogeneous data centers with lots of different chips inside, and we’ll compile workloads to the different chips inside the data centers.”
When software becomes stable, economics attempts to drive down costs, but when software evolves rapidly, it calls for more innovation in hardware to keep up. “It is a balance between saying we need it faster, versus building the best combination of product for the best power consumption, for the best performance,” says Frank Schirrmeister, executive director of strategic programs for system solutions at Synopsys. “The hyperscalers talk a lot about this, and one of the main reasons for them to build their own chips and their own accelerators is for co-optimization of KPIs. It may be performance. It may be power. We may be at a point where that dynamic shifts. They say we need it fast, but it’s now equally important, or even more important, that it has the right power and the right performance.”
The challenge is determining how much customization worthwhile, economically and from a power/performance standpoint, and for whom, and sometimes that line isn’t always clear. “The specs are getting very complicated,” said Purna Mohanty, CEO of SignatureIP. “Sometimes, the customer may not be able to even articulate what they want, because they want everything in the world. That’s not possible, of course. But at the same time, you have to make sure you are in alignment with the customer. We initially wanted to sell off-the-shelf IP, because you can’t reinvent the wheel for every customer. But the flip side is that it’s rewarding to work with leading-edge customers that bring a lot of value to you, and you’re adding new features to your IP. So it’s kind of a give-and-take.”
Still, each time the pendulum swings, the demands on tools change. “We have been building better hardware to make the software run better,” says MIPS’ Grove. “There is an inversion of that model now because software is changing so fast, the workloads, whether it be different model architectures for these applications or otherwise, is outpacing the speed at which the hardware development flow takes place. Understanding the software as you build the hardware is fundamentally an inversion in that model. In that model you just add more accelerators here or there to make that software work better. Now it becomes, ‘What is the software doing, and how do we partition and deploy this on different elements in the system?'”
Some of the changes can best be seen by looking at RISC-V. “Companies are optimizing silicon based on the workload that it’s targeting,” says Andrea Gallo, CEO for RISC-V International. “We are in the era of workload-designed silicon.”
But when you dig into the surrounding ecosystem, you see a tiny internal wave where companies develop extensions to the core to improve power or performance. This requires them to build parts from their own ecosystem, such as compilers. When they no longer get enough benefit from that proprietary extension to cover the cost of tool maintenance, they will seek to spread the costs by sharing it with everyone else and reverting to standardization.
“When you use the vendor or custom op codes, you own the complete cost of ownership,” adds RISC-V International’s Gallo. “It’s on you, because you have a custom toolchain and custom software integration. This gives you very fast innovation, but the next step would be to propose your custom extensions to become standards. Then the cost of ownership is shared across the entire ecosystem.”
When you know the workloads, you can do better than generic. “Knowing the expected software workload at the time of defining the functional specs for a chip has enabled specialization of the processing elements within SoCs,” says Quadric’s Roddy. “Processors didn’t need to be generic. They could be application-tailored. RISC-V didn’t invent the idea of tailoring a processor to a target workload. Tensilica began 15 years before RISC-V and has fully automated the creation of custom cores and accompanying toolsets. RISC-V adopted that concept and made it non-proprietary.”
In between, there is a mix of both. “If you try and run arbitrary software, you don’t have any of those insights into the workload,” says MIPS’ Murphy. “That’s where, especially on the AI compute side, we need to focus on making sure that the generic compute engines — the vector machines, the matrix machines, the things that actually execute AI-style workloads with big matrix operations — are built generically, and scalable enough that they can have good-enough performance on an arbitrary workload, even if it’s garbled slop from AI.”
Energy and thermal
A common theme pushing everyone toward co-design is energy. On the edge, that means extending battery life as much as possible. In the data centers it is about managing the heat that comes from consumption of that energy. That might make you think that energy has become a primary design factor. “The first thing anyone considers is does it work functionally,” says Grove. “Then, does it work in the period of time or in the window that it needs to? Now there’s probably some heavy lifting that happens there. Finally, what does it mean to be deployed in the field? All of these are dramatically impacted by software. While software engineers probably understand issues about power, they are not equipped with the tools they need to understand it early enough. But power is probably step three on the journey of getting something out into market.”
That needs to change. “If a software engineer is writing things purely for performance and does not know what power is, that is a problem,” says Murphy. “We are building tools and infrastructure to make sure that as they are developing that software alongside their hardware, they are getting power numbers and are optimizing their workloads. We need to make sure we are providing targeted hardware that’s optimizing for things like TOPS per watt instead of raw TOPS.”
Understanding performance and power is far from trivial. “We understand that it is a challenge, especially for heterogeneous applications with multi-level caching,” says Meier. “It is possible they will never fully understand it, but that’s where power/performance tradeoffs happen. We understand this is a problem and there is a lot of analysis that goes on. It is ripe for EDA tooling to continue to look for ways to improve and help our customers design more efficient silicon.”
The problem continues to get tougher. “The complexity of what you can actually grasp with new tooling goes well beyond hardware and software,” says Synopsys’ Schirrmeister. “You may find hardware and software engineers uniting because they now have to deal with those pesky mechanical and electromagnetic and multiphysics guys taking software, taking hardware on the chip, and now looking at thermal. Now the hardware-software unit becomes the new element to which multiphysics is attached to assess the combination of both. Now we can deal with that complexity by virtue of organization bringing them together, but also by virtue of just complexity — being able to grasp in a long workload, based on all the activity data created by software, which parts of the chip I need to look further for IR drop aspects and things like that.”
To make life a little more complicated, hardware is not just having to deal with workloads coming from software. There are other functions that hardware performs, and these also have to be factored into some aspects of hardware design. “If we think about it as a power performance analysis, how do we capture that in the context of a realistic workload?” says Meier. “It also works in areas outside of what we would consider a software workload. It’s still a workload, but it includes areas like DFT, understanding from a DFT context power and performance, and what happens there.”
Some people have suggested that AI itself may be able to understand the complex relationships between hardware/software and power/performance. “If we look at the LLMs, everything that we work on today, we think about where the knowledge came from that they’ve been trained on,” says Grove. “Textbooks, repositories, public knowledge on the internet. How do we become power aware? How do these coding agents or other things actually become aware? Where does that data set live? Where is the data set for this software that ran and consumed this much power, whether it’s at the chip level, the server rack level, the box level, the car level, the data center level?”
Until AI-driven co-design is ready, solutions may again go back to integration of IPs. “Consider matrix extensions,” says Gallo. “We have three working groups in parallel on three different options, because we believe that one matrix extension doesn’t fit all. We have one extension that is a set of operations on top of the vector extensions. It’s very tiny. They are not adding additional accumulators, and so the power consumption is very small. Then, on the other extreme case, there is a full-blown set of matrix registers and operations and accumulators. Those provide the highest throughput, the fastest operations, because you have all the accumulators and you can work on larger matrices. When you start adding that many registers for matrix, die size and power consumption increase. Initially I thought the small one was for IoT devices and the full-blown matrix accelerator was for supercomputers. Then the experts start telling me, it may even be the opposite. If you are designing an edge AI chipset, you have few cores and possibly a single matrix accelerator that is shared, so you would use the large matrix accelerator shared among multiple cores for edge AI. With a mass replication of cores, maybe you want a small matrix capability in each core rather than being shared.”
[Editor’s Note: Part two will explore what co-design solutions look like today, the gaps that need to be filled, and the long-term implications of these changes.]

articles.title: Ergonomic Hacks for Sedentary Tech Workers - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Tech work keeps software developers and system engineers attached to desk stations for 8 to 12 hours a day. Long desk sessions slowly take a toll on physical health, leading to tight joints and sluggish energy levels.
Small workplace upgrades create dramatic shifts in daily comfort and focus. Adopting smart ergonomic habits keeps your body resilient without sacrificing daily coding productivity.
Optimizing Monitor Placement for Neck Comfort
Staring down at a low screen causes severe strain on upper back muscles during long work hours. Positioning your monitor at eye level prevents neck strain and maintains optimal spinal alignment throughout long working hours. Correct height alignment stops developers from slumping forward during long coding sprints.
Keep the display about an arm’s length away to protect against severe eye fatigue. Adjusting screen brightness to match ambient room lighting keeps your vision sharp throughout the day. Simple monitor arms permit quick height adjustments across different work tasks.
Dual monitors require extra attention to prevent constant neck twisting throughout long shifts. Center the primary monitor directly in front of your main keyboard setup. Place secondary displays off to the side at identical height angles for smooth viewing.
Upgrading Desk Setup and Leg Support
Sitting in standard office chairs for extended periods restricts blood flow down to lower extremities. Many tech professionals rely on options such as compression stockings Australia to keep lower limb circulation steady throughout long workdays. Quality gear prevents fluid buildup and maintains leg comfort during marathon programming sessions.
Footrests offer targeted relief by supporting proper knee and hip alignment. Elevating your feet slightly reduces lower back pressure and keeps thighs parallel to the ground. Adjusting desk height permits your shoulders to relax completely.
Clear physical clutter from beneath your primary desk area. Ample legroom permits frequent position shifts throughout long work shifts. Freeing up leg space encourages natural stretching between coding tasks.
Selecting Supportive Chairs for Spinal Health
Quality office seating plays a foundational role in maintaining spine health over long desk shifts. Proper lumbar support maintains the natural inward curve of the lower spine. Adjustable backrests distribute body weight evenly across the entire chair base.
Adjustable armrests keep wrists level with your keyboard surface. Ergonomic seating features include:
- Seat depth controls to protect knee circulation
- Dynamic lumbar adjustments for spine support
- Pneumatic height controls for custom alignment
- Adjustable tilt tension to balance upper body support.
Proper armrest height stops shoulder tension from building up during deep work sessions.
Mesh chair backing promotes airflow to keep you cool during intense work hours. Cushioned seat pans prevent uncomfortable pressure points around hip joints. Reclining slightly backward reduces spinal disc compression during long code review sessions.
Managing Digital Eye Strain and Lighting
Screen glare forces eye muscles to work double time during dark evening shifts. Shift your workspace relative to windows to minimize harsh background reflections. Soft ambient room light reduces sharp contrast between monitors and surrounding walls.
Taking periodic breaks from monitor screens helps maintain visual comfort. Resting your eyes every 20 minutes keeps focusing muscles relaxed. Periodic blinking maintains surface hydration and protects eye comfort.
Font sizes on code editors need generous scaling for physical comfort. Enlarging code text prevents leaning forward toward high-resolution screens. Dark mode themes lower glare when coding late into the night.
Modern tech careers require proactive habits to safeguard physical health. Simple adjustments to workspace tools make daily desk routines far more comfortable.
Consistent attention to posture and movement builds lasting energy. Small daily changes preserve your physical well-being throughout long programming sessions.

articles.title: New Disrupt Africa Intelligence offering to assist VCs, corporates in accessing continent’s startup ecosystem - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Tech news and research platform Disrupt Africa has launched “Disrupt Intelligence”, which offers corporates and VC looking to engage – or further engage – with the African tech market access to signals, founder intelligence, sector research and selective scouting support.
Launched in 2014 by Tom Jackson and Gabriella Mulligan, Disrupt Africa is one of Africa’s most recognisable technology ecosystem media brands. The platform combines startup news, funding intelligence, ecosystem commentary, research publications, podcast content, and a proprietary database of more than 3,000 African technology ventures.
“African technology markets remain attractive, but fragmented, unevenly documented, and difficult for external organisations to read accurately. Investors, DFIs, accelerators, corporates and ecosystem builders need credible signals before committing capital, partnership resources, programme budgets, or market-entry effort,” Disrupt Africa co-founder Tom Jackson said.
Enter Disrupt Africa Intelligence, which helps organisations make better African tech ecosystem decisions through trusted market signals, founder intelligence, sector research, and selective scouting support. The recommended starting point is a 90-day pilot designed to prove value quickly before any longer-term retainer, research mandate, or partnership.
Why Disrupt Africa?
| 15 years African tech ecosystem experience | 80+ podcasts Founder, investor and ecosystem conversations | 30 research publications Including 11 African Tech Startups Funding Reports | 3,000+ ventures Startup database and trusted founder/funder relationships | 
The problems Disrupt Africa helps you solve:
- We need to understand African tech markets before committing capital, partnerships or programme resources.
- We need credible startup signals beyond pitch decks, PR and LinkedIn noise.
- We need a trusted intelligence partner who already understands the founder, funder and ecosystem landscape.
Products
| Product | Best for | What the client gets | Decision supported | Price / duration | 
| Monthly Signal Briefing | Funds, DFIs, accelerators or corporates needing a current market read. | One monthly memo; one 60-minute briefing call; top funding, founder, sector and ecosystem signals; one agreed theme. | Whether to investigate, enter, pause or deepen activity in a market or theme. | US$3,000-4,000 per month | 
| Disrupt Africa Intelligence Retainer | Organisations with ongoing Africa tech exposure or programme responsibility. | Monthly memo; briefing call; ongoing signal tracking; founder/funder context; market-entry or ecosystem engagement advice; quarterly opportunity and risk review. | How to allocate attention, capital, partnership effort or programme resources. | US$5,000-8,000 per month | 
| Sector or Country Specific Intelligence Sprint | Teams assessing a defined market, vertical, funding pattern or investment theme. | Agreed country, sector or theme; ecosystem map; founder/funder context notes; final briefing; recommended engagement route. | Whether and how to proceed with a market, sector or investment thesis. | US$10,000-20,000 / 4-6 weeks | 
| Startup Scouting and Signal Mapping | Corporates, funds and accelerators seeking credible startup discovery. | Agreed country, sector or theme; screened startup longlist; ecosystem map; founder/funder context notes; final briefing; recommended engagement route. | Which ventures are relevant, credible and worth deeper engagement. | US$10,000-20,000 / 4-6 weeks | 
| Disrupt Africa Visibility Services | Organisations seeking targeted ecosystem visibility with clear labelling. | Podcast, newsletter and report sponsorships, structured separately from editorial coverage. | How to reach an African tech audience while preserving trust and transparency. | Priced on request | 
Operating guardrails
Disrupt Africa sells intelligence, context and structured signal, not guaranteed access or editorial influence. Introductions are selective and made only where and when considered appropriate. Visibility products are always labelled and kept visibly separate from independent editorial judgement.

articles.title: Samsung transforme ses Galaxy Buds en aides auditives : pourquoi la France reste à l'écart
articles.text:
Feu vert de la FDA pour les Galaxy Buds 3 Pro et 4 Pro, qui deviennent des aides auditives sans ordonnance. Lancement au quatrième trimestre 2026 aux États-Unis. En Europe, Apple a déjà ouvert la voie ; la France, elle, n'a toujours pas suivi.
Cinq minutes pour un audiogramme, directement dans les réglages des Buds
Deux fonctions. Hearing Test, enregistrée comme Software as a Medical Device, réalise une audiométrie tonale pure oreille par oreille et classe l'audition en cinq catégories, en cinq minutes, depuis les réglages des Buds. Hearing Aid exploite ensuite l'audiogramme pour personnaliser l'amplification, avec suppression de bruit et beamforming acoustique.
Samsung revendique une précision comparable à celle d'un audiologiste et cite des études de validation menées au Vanderbilt University Medical Center, à San Jose State University et à l'Université de Memphis. Le réglage s'appuie sur NAL-NL2, standard clinique conçu par les National Acoustic Laboratories — l'organisme australien avec lequel Samsung a précisément co-développé la fonction.
Une mise à jour suffit pour transformer des écouteurs en dispositif médical
C'est là que la frontière bouge. Samsung n'a pas besoin de lancer un appareil dédié : les fonctions seront intégrées aux Galaxy Buds3 Pro et Buds4 Pro compatibles, avec un Galaxy sous One UI 8 ou ultérieur. Du matériel grand public déjà vendu devient un dispositif médical certifié, par logiciel.
Aux États-Unis, l'argument économique est massif : environ 250 dollars pour une paire de Buds 4 Pro, contre plusieurs milliers pour un appareillage sur ordonnance. La FDA avait ouvert la brèche en créant la catégorie OTC en 2022 ; Apple a obtenu son autorisation en septembre 2024.
L'obstacle n'est plus européen
Apple a démontré que le marquage CE Dispositif Médical n'était pas le mur annoncé : sa fonction d'aide auditive est active sur plusieurs marchés européens depuis février 2025. Pas en France, où seul le test auditif est accessible, malgré des discussions engagées fin 2024 avec les autorités sanitaires.
Deux raisons. D'abord un cadre juridique strict : le Code de la santé publique réserve l'appareillage des déficients de l'ouïe aux audioprothésistes diplômés. Ensuite, et surtout, le contexte économique français est également très différent de celui des États-Unis. Avec le 100 % Santé, une offre d'aides auditives de classe I peut déjà être proposée sans reste à charge aux assurés éligibles. L'argument de démocratisation par le prix, central outre-Atlantique, est donc moins évident en France.
Samsung vise pour l'instant les États-Unis et « certains marchés approuvés », sans les détailler. Pour la France, aucune disponibilité n'est annoncée

articles.title: Dans notre coup de cœur PS5 de l’année (noté 9/10) l’éclipse transforme le monde en cauchemar
articles.text:
Ce mercredi 12 août 2026, une éclipse solaire partielle est visible depuis la France. Un phénomène exceptionnel qui trouve un écho inattendu dans Saros, dans lequel vous incarnez Arjun Devraj, un exécuteur Soltari envoyé sur Carcosa, une planète mystérieuse et particulièrement hostile, plongée sous la lumière permanente d’une éclipse. L’événement n’a d’ailleurs jamais été aussi bien représenté que dans Saros, où les effets de lumière sont le terrain d’expérimentation d’un studio qui maîtrise parfaitement son moteur graphique.
Si vous avez aimé Returnal, difficile de ne pas avoir envie de mettre les mains sur Saros. Développé par Housemarque, le titre reprend les grandes bases de son prédécesseur : une aventure d’action à la troisième personne, une structure roguelite et des affrontements extrêmement nerveux où les projectiles envahissent littéralement l’écran.
Le jeu est une exclusivité PS5, habituellement vendue 79,99 € sur le PlayStation Store, mais il est proposé à 59,99 € jusqu’au 13 août 2026 (soit -25 %), achetable directement sur le PS Store, ou via une carte cadeau PSN de 60 €. Il est également disponible en version physique chez plusieurs e-commerçants.
C’est quoi, Saros ?
Développé par Housemarque, le studio derrière Returnal, Saros est un jeu d’action à la troisième personne exclusivement disponible sur PS5. Le jeu se déroule sur Carcosa, une planète mystérieuse qui évolue au fil des cycles et semble obéir à des règles qui échappent à celles et ceux qui tentent de l’explorer. Au cœur de ce monde étrange, une éclipse permanente transforme progressivement l’environnement, l’atmosphère se pare d’une belle lumière dorée, mais rend la faune encore plus dangereuse. Ici, mourir n’est pas la fin, mais le début d’une nouvelle tentative.
Comme tout bon roguelite, chaque échec permet à Arjun de revenir plus puissant, avec une progression permanente qui rend les prochaines tentatives plus accessibles. Housemarque conserve également le « bullet hell », ce déluge de projectiles aussi impressionnant que dangereux.
À ce prix, Saros est-il une bonne affaire ?
Saros n’est clairement pas le jeu le moins cher de la PS5, mais son gameplay particulièrement nerveux, son histoire bien construite et ses graphismes qui en mettent plein les yeux valent l’investissement, si le genre du roguelite vous parle. Les affrontements sont rapides, exigeants et donnent une vraie sensation de maîtrise une fois les déplacements et les esquives assimilés. La boucle roguelite, pensée autour de la répétition et de la progression permanente, donne également envie de relancer une partie après chaque échec.
Le jeu constitue également une belle vitrine technique pour la PS5, et plus encore pour la PS5 Pro. Les effets de lumière, les environnements et les innombrables projectiles affichés simultanément à l’écran donnent lieu à des scènes spectaculaires, sans sacrifier la fluidité. Saros s’adresse surtout aux joueuses et aux joueurs qui cherchent une grosse expérience d’action et veulent profiter d’un jeu capable de montrer ce que la console de Sony a dans le ventre.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (August 12, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (August 12, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Wednesday, August 12, 2026.
From Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran stepping down to EV mobility service startup Yulu raising $93 million, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Latest news
Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran steps down
Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran has stepped down from his role and will not seek reappointment due to lack of unanimity from the board members on his continuation.
Chandrasekaran was appointed the chairman of Tata Sons, the holding company of the $400-billion Tata Group, in February 2017.
Ola Electric secures 5-year PLI window
Ola Electric has secured a revised timeline under the Government’s Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for advanced chemistry cells (ACC). The company secured a full five-year PLI window through calendar year 2031 and cumulative incentives of up to Rs 7,240 crore, the company said in a BSE filing.
Funding news
Yulu raises $93M led by GEF Capital
Electric mobility-as-a-service (MaaS) startup Yulu has raised $93 million in a Series C funding round. The total includes equity of $63 million, led by GEF Capital Partners, with the remaining $30 million raised via debt.
According to Yulu, this is its largest funding round and it will use the capital to quadruple its active fleet to 200,000 electric vehicles (EVs) in the next two years, expand service hubs, and deepen strategic enterprise partnerships.
Wippi raises $1.2M to scale screen-free AI products for children
Wippi has raised $1.2 million in seed funding led by 12 Flags, with participation from Warmup Ventures, Ventana Ventures and Ruvento Ventures. The Bengaluru-based children's technology startup will use the capital to develop its voice AI, expand engineering and AI teams, scale manufacturing in India and grow its direct-to-consumer business.
Founded by Rishabh Singhi and Siddhartha Jain, Wippi builds screen-free, conversational products combining voice AI, Character Cards, illustrated storybooks and interactive storytelling. The company plans to expand its characters, languages and content, introduce collectible figurines and reach more than 15,000 families over the next 12 months.
Lane raises Rs 8.5 Cr to expand structured driver education
Tech-enabled driving education platform Lane has raised Rs 8.5 crore in a funding round led by Kae Capital, with participation from DeVC, Antler India, Panthera Peak and angel investors. Founded in 2025 by Samiksha Agarwal, Lane provides structured driving instruction and has delivered more than 30,000 hours of training to over 3,100 learners. Nearly 70% of its customers already held driving licences.
The company will use the funding to expand its instructor network, develop sensor-based driving behaviour technology and build services supporting car ownership. Lane plans to expand across Bengaluru and other Tier 1 cities.
Quarkitech raises Rs 2 Cr to develop sensor data compression technology
Quarkitech, a deeptech company based at IIT Madras Research Park, has raised Rs 2 crore in pre-seed funding from Artha Access and Finvolve to develop proprietary data compression technology for defence, aerospace and other data-intensive applications. It has also received a Rs 1.5 crore grant under the National Quantum Mission.
Its software compresses sensor data at source by 10-100 times, targeting radar, LiDAR, hyperspectral and electro-optical systems on UAVs, satellites and other platforms. In laboratory testing, Quarkitech reports 26x data reduction while retaining 98% of mission-critical information. It is now validating the technology under real-world operating conditions.
KshatraLabs secures investment to advance autonomous counter-drone systems
KshatraLabs has received an undisclosed investment from Finvolve and India Accelerator to advance its autonomous counter-drone technology. Its HAWK interceptor is designed to detect, track and neutralise hostile UAVs at speeds of up to 300 km/h, with less than five seconds of launch readiness.
The company is developing swarm-capable systems supported by its APEX autonomy stack and an AI-native C4ISR and JADC2 layer for multi-sensor fusion and operations in GPS-denied environments. KshatraLabs has demonstrated autonomous interception and hardware-in-the-loop testing at 90 m/s. The funding will support engineering, R&D, certifications and field validation, with the company targeting TRL-6.
Other news
PayU launches RBI-compliant accessible payment checkout
PayU has launched an accessible payment checkout designed for blind and visually impaired users, which it says is India's first RBI-compliant checkout of its kind. The solution complies with the Reserve Bank of India's October 2024 accessibility mandate under BIS IS 17802 and is designed to improve navigation and interaction for users with visual and cognitive accessibility needs.
Features include full screen-reader optimisation, adjustable user profiles, visual modes for low vision and colour blindness, and text resizing up to 200%. Users can navigate payment methods, confirm amounts and complete transactions through screen-reader assistance without sighted support.
BLive, Tata Motors partner to deploy 1,000 electric mini trucks
BLive has signed an MoU with Tata Motors to deploy up to 1,000 Tata electric mini trucks through its BLive PRIME franchise-owned fleet programme. The first batch of Tata Ace Pro EVs has already been inducted for enterprise logistics operations. BLive plans to deploy the fleets across sectors including e-commerce, quick commerce, manufacturing, retail distribution, pharmaceuticals and 3PL.
Under the model, franchise partners own the vehicles, while BLive manages enterprise demand, deployment, charging, maintenance, technology and operations. The company has committed Rs 100 crore to BLive PRIME and said franchise investments start at about Rs 45 lakh.
i-Hub Gujarat and SanchiConnect expand deeptech acceleration
i-Hub Gujarat and SanchiConnect are expanding their TattvaX partnership to support deeptech startups in strategically important sectors, including defence, drones and space. Following the programme, the partners are launching sector-focused accelerators, with initiatives in drones and aerospace already underway.
The model connects startups with investors, industry buyers and government stakeholders, including police departments, municipal corporations and regional PSUs, to help move technologies from development towards deployment. SanchiConnect is also building sector-focused micro-ecosystems with state governments, industry associations and incubators. A recent Demo Day brought together 30 startups, more than 20 investors and corporate leaders over two days.
TimbuckDo to create Rs 25 lakh in student gig opportunities
TimbuckDo has partnered with IdeaBaaz Startup Fest as workforce partner, creating Rs 25 lakh in gig opportunities for more than 100 students during the five-day festival from August 26-30, 2026, at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. Students will support festival operations while working alongside startups, entrepreneurs and investors, gaining practical experience and industry exposure.
The partnership builds on TimbuckDo's earlier appearance on IdeaBaaz as a startup seeking funding. The company says the initiative reflects its focus on student gig work as a route to earning, practical experience and participation in India's startup ecosystem.
Glu appoints Neha Sharma Katyal as Head of Growth - India
Glu has appointed Neha Sharma Katyal as Head of Growth - India to lead market expansion, growth strategy and strategic partnerships. Reporting to founder and CEO Rahul Pandey, she will drive go-to-market, customer acquisition and commercial development as AI assistants and conversational search reshape brand discovery.
Katyal brings more than 18 years of experience across digital media, advertising and technology, with senior roles at Disney+ Hotstar, The Trade Desk, Spotify and Twitter. Glu helps brands improve visibility and influence across AI-powered buying journeys and works with brands including Heads Up For Tails, 11:11, Dilmah Tea and Tasc Performance.
Walplast takes majority stake in Vura Bau Chemie
Walplast Products has made a strategic majority investment in Vura Bau Chemie, strengthening its presence across specialised building materials. Vura manufactures tile adhesives, waterproofing solutions and stone-care products, with a focus on quality and technical expertise. The investment will expand Walplast’s offerings in tile adhesives and waterproofing, add stone-care products and support entry into new market segments.
It also complements Walplast’s manufacturing, R&D and distribution capabilities as it expands across India’s construction materials value chain. The companies said the investment is intended to support category expansion and address evolving demand in India’s housing and infrastructure sectors.
India leads Asia-Pacific in demand for digital skills
India is the most digitally intensive hiring market among six Asia-Pacific economies studied by Indeed Hiring Lab and the Asian Development Bank. Nearly 9 in 10 Indian job postings require digital skills, while more than half require intermediate or advanced proficiency. The demand spans sectors including education, insurance, healthcare, construction and retail.
Digital skills also carry a wage premium, with advanced skills associated with 31% higher pay than comparable roles requiring none, versus 12% for intermediate and 5% for basic skills. AI requirements are also rising, with advanced-digital roles increasingly seeking AI capabilities and additional wage premiums for AI skills.
UpTik nearly doubles AUM to Rs 20 Cr
UpTik, the invoice financing investment platform of Growwcap Fintech, has nearly doubled its AUM to Rs 20 crore from Rs 10 crore at FY26-end. The platform recorded more than Rs 10 crore in retail investments during July, alongside its highest monthly app downloads and largest addition of new investors since launch.
UpTik connects investors with opportunities backed by approved business invoices while helping MSMEs access working capital. It has recorded more than 5,000 app downloads and 30-40% monthly growth in investor participation. The platform plans to expand its investor base and strengthen its digital infrastructure.
Pathway reports low-cost reasoning results and raises funding
Pathway has published benchmark results for BDH-CQ, a 150-million-parameter reasoning model, which scored 29.5% pass@2 on ARC-AGI-1 at a reported $0.0007 per task. The company says BDH-CQ uses recurrent latent-state reasoning rather than generating intermediate text traces, reducing inference costs.
Pathway has also secured additional funding at a $500 million valuation, taking total seed funding to $30 million. The capital will primarily expand compute capacity, including GB300 systems. The company has appointed Adam Kurzrok, formerly a Google DeepMind Gemini product leader, as chief product officer and plans to expand its reasoning models and benchmarks.
Jee Bhar Ke targets Rs 150-200 Cr business
RASA Group is investing Rs 15 crore to expand its cloud kitchen brand Jee Bhar Ke, targeting a Rs 150-200 crore business over five years. The company plans up to eight new kitchens across North and Central India over the next 12-24 months, with expansion planned across cities including Jaipur, Lucknow, Chandigarh, Indore and Jammu.
Currently operating in Delhi, Gurugram and Noida, Jee Bhar Ke fulfils about 10,000 orders monthly, with 35-40% repeat customers. The investment will fund kitchen expansion, operations and technology. The brand aims to contribute 10-15% of RASA Group's revenue over the coming years.
(This article will be updated with the latest news throughout the day.)

articles.title: Comment suivre l'éclipse du 12 août 2026 en direct ?
articles.text:
Un phénomène rare est sur le point de se produire en France : la Lune va passer devant le Soleil. S’il est question d’une éclipse partielle, le spectacle s’annonce impressionnant avec des niveaux d’occultation entre 89 % et 99 %, en fonction de la région où vous vous situez. Si vous n’avez pas l’opportunité d’assister à l’événement en extérieur, plusieurs agences et organismes diffusent l’événement en direct.
La Lune va passer devant le Soleil
Pour rappel, la dernière éclipse solaire totale visible depuis la France remonte au 11 août 1999. Précisément 27 ans plus tard, soit ce 12 août 2026, une nouvelle éclipse solaire se produira, mais elle sera cette fois-ci partielle. En effet, si le nord de l’Espagne et une bande étroite de l’Islande pourront profiter d’une éclipse totale, l’Hexagone pourra tout de même assister à une éclipse partielle qui s’annonce spectaculaire. À titre d’exemple, les niveaux d’occultation dans ces différentes villes seront les suivants : 89,9 % à Strasbourg, 92,2 % à Paris, 92 % à Lille, 96,3 % à Marseille ou encore 99 % à Biarritz.
Les horaires de l’éclipse varient selon la région où vous vous trouvez. À Paris, par exemple, elle débutera à 19 h 22, atteindra son maximum à 20 h 17 et prendra fin à 21 h 09. Rappelons également l’importance de porter des lunettes d’éclipse certifiées ISO 12312-2 et récentes pour observer le phénomène en toute sécurité. Regarder directement le Soleil à l’œil nu, même pendant quelques secondes, peut provoquer des lésions rétiniennes irréversibles. Aussi, faites attention à certains réglages de votre smartphone si vous comptez immortaliser l’événement. Si vous n’avez pas l’occasion d’assister à l’événement en extérieur, pas d’inquiétude : plusieurs organismes et agences le diffuseront en direct.
Comment suivre l’événement en direct ?
Sans surprise, la NASA propose une retransmission en direct, à partir de 19 h 15, avec des interventions de scientifiques pour tenter de mieux comprendre l’événement. C’est l’idéal pour suivre l’éclipse à la maison.
L’Agence spatiale européenne (ESA) a quant à elle placé ses caméras dans l’Observatoire Astrofísico de Javalambre, situé dans la province de Teruel (Espagne). Elle propose deux retransmissions en direct de l’événement. La première, nommée Telescopic Feed, retransmet le phénomène en direct, sans aucun commentaire, dans un silence total. La seconde, que vous retrouverez ci-dessous, retransmet l’événement avec des interventions d’experts.
Il ne reste maintenant plus qu’à patienter pour suivre cet événement rare en direct. À noter que la prochaine éclipse solaire visible depuis la France aura lieu le 2 août 2027. Elle sera toutefois nettement moins importante que celle de ce 12 août 2026, avec une occultation d’environ 51 % à Paris et pouvant atteindre 80 % à Perpignan. Il faudra attendre le 3 septembre 2081 pour assister à une éclipse solaire totale visible depuis la France.

articles.title: FBI: Hackers target online accounts to steal nude photos
articles.text:
The FBI warns that cybercriminals are targeting adults' and children's social media and other online accounts to steal sexually explicit images or videos.
As the law enforcement agency explained in a public service announcement published this week, the attackers may use the stolen content to blackmail the victims or try to sell it on criminal marketplaces.
They may also share the victims' personal information (including names, dates of birth, emails, phone numbers, and social media usernames) with other criminals, who can use it to pressure them into providing additional private images and videos through sextortion.
Sextortion is a form of online blackmail in which cybercriminals threaten victims with publicly leaking nude images and videos they stole (through hacking) or obtained (through coercion). In some cases, they may also demand payment not to leak the explicit content online or share it with the targets' family and friends.
"Once the sexually explicit content is stolen, SE actors post or sell it to criminal marketplaces, which often includes personal information about the victim and typically without their knowledge," the FBI warned.
"As a result, victims often face re-victimization through harassment, sextortion, stalking or other targeted attacks, such as advertising stolen content on a victim's own social media page."
Student-athletes also targeted by sexual exploitation schemes
The same day, the FBI and the National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) have also warned that cybercriminals are targeting student-athletes' online accounts in similar sexual exploitation schemes and asked coaches, compliance staff, and athletic department leadership to raise awareness within their schools and communities.
It also told potential victims not to reply to text messages or emails asking them to provide verification codes or click password reset links and advised against storing explicit photos or videos on social media accounts or Internet-accessible sites. Additionally, it recommended using complex passwords and enabling multi-factor authentication whenever possible.
"The FBI has identified several indicators associated with these schemes, including, unsolicited text messages claiming an account will be disabled absent a verification code and unsolicited emails referencing a new login with an embedded link to reset a password," it said.
"The FBI advises that a legitimate platform or service will not request a verification code, temporary password, or PIN reset code from an account holder. Utilizing passwords and PINs that do not include personal information, such as names, dates or birth and other easily accessible information, can also help lower the risk of victimization."
While the FBI hasn't shared what prompted this alert, the bureau often issues public service announcements after noticing an increase in the incidents they address.
Almost five years ago, in September 2021, it also warned of a massive increase in sextortion complaints and advised those receiving threats to stop all interaction with the criminals immediately and contact law enforcement as soon as possible.
Sextortionists face dozens of years in prison if caught and sentenced. For instance, in May, a Canadian man was sentenced to 33 years in prison for targeting more than 145 children across the United States, some as young as 6 years old, in an eight-year-long sextortion scheme.

articles.title: WhatsApp Unveils New Scam Alert Feature
articles.text:
WhatsApp has begun a limited beta rollout of Scam Alert, an optional feature that uses an on-device machine learning model to flag suspicious messages from non-contacts.
The company says the tool is designed to work alongside end-to-end encryption rather than around it, with classification happening entirely on the device and no automatic reporting to WhatsApp or parent company Meta.
Once a user enables the feature, a model is downloaded to the device and evaluates incoming messages for patterns associated with known scams, drawing on conversational structure and linguistic cues.
If a message is flagged, only the recipient sees a warning inside the chat, but the sender is not notified. The user can block the contact, report the message, ignore the warning, or mark the conversation as trusted so future alerts are suppressed. Users who mark a chat as trusted can separately choose to share the last five messages received to help refine the model’s accuracy.
To prevent a scenario where a specific model could be pushed to a specific person, WhatsApp says every model release must be logged on a third-party, append-only transparency ledger before it can be distributed.
Each release is accompanied by a manifest of SHA-256 hashes covering the model weights and related files, with the manifest digest signed using Ed25519 keys held by Cloudflare rather than Meta. Devices verify this signature, cross-check it against the ledger, and confirm the downloaded files match the published hashes before the model is allowed to run.
Because no message content leaves the device, WhatsApp still needs a way to gauge whether the feature is functioning correctly. For that, it built what it calls a confidential federated analytics pipeline, which collects only two categories of data: counts of how often warnings were triggered and counts of what action users took afterward, such as blocking or marking a chat as trusted.
WhatsApp outlines a threat model covering external attackers, compromised infrastructure insiders, and supply-chain risk, and says the pipeline’s defenses are meant to ensure that targeting a single user’s data would require compromising the entire system.
On the verification side, users will be able to review a transparency log in the app, accessible through Account > Request Info > Scam Alert Activity, showing which messages were scanned, the outcome, and which model version made the call.
WhatsApp also says it is expanding its bug bounty program to cover Scam Alert, and researchers stress-tested the system ahead of the beta rollout.
The company characterizes the release as an early technical preview rather than a finished product, noting the feature will continue to evolve during the beta period based on researcher and user feedback before any wider rollout.
Signal announces automatic key verification
Signal has introduced automatic key verification, a new feature meant to complement its existing safety number system by confirming that no unauthorized party sits between two users in an end-to-end encrypted conversation.
Unlike manual safety number checks, which require an in-person meeting or a secondary communication channel, the new system performs verification independently through checks carried out by the user, their contact, and third-party auditors.
The feature is designed to catch scenarios where a Signal account’s public key gets swapped without the owner’s knowledge. This can happen, for instance, if an attacker compromised Signal’s infrastructure and linked a different key to a target’s phone number.
Users can trigger a check from a connection’s profile by opening ‘View Safety Number’ and tapping ‘Verify automatically’ under the Automatic Key Verification heading. A green checkmark reading ‘Encryption verified’ confirms a match.
Underpinning the feature is a system Signal calls key transparency, which records every registration, phone number change, and username change in a cryptographically verifiable log.
Cloudflare and Trail of Bits act as independent auditors of this log. All identifiers and keys in the log are obscured using a verifiable random function and a keyed hash function, so the auditors themselves never see plaintext user data.
The feature is opt-out. Users who don’t want to rely on Signal or its auditors can disable it under Privacy > Advanced > Automatic Key Verification and continue relying solely on manual safety number checks.

articles.title: Google enrichit les Pixel Buds Pro 2 et Pixel Buds 2a avec l'IA Gemini — Frandroid
articles.text:
En plus des nouveaux smartphones Google Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro XL et Pixel 11 Pro Fold, le géant américain a présenté de nouvelles fonctionnalités pour ses écouteurs intra-auriculaires. Ainsi, les Pixel Buds Pro 2 vont désormais bénéficier d’une réduction de bruit active dite « dynamique ».
Concrètement, le dispositif détecte les variations subtiles dans l’étanchéité acoustique de l’écouteur, par exemple lorsque celui-ci bouge légèrement dans l’oreille, et ajuste automatiquement le traitement du signal pour maintenir une performance constante.
    Pour aller plus loin
            Quels sont les meilleurs écouteurs sans fil en 2026 ?
            
Cette fonction entend corriger un défaut courant chez les écouteurs intra-auriculaires, dont l’efficacité de l’annulation de bruit dépend fortement de la qualité de « l’installation » dans le conduit auditif. Ici, cette adaptation se fait sans intervention de l’utilisateur, contrairement à certains concurrents qui nécessitent une reconfiguration manuelle après chaque insertion.
Gemini prend le contrôle vocal des réglages
L’autre nouveauté majeure concerne l’intégration renforcée de l’assistant Gemini. Il est désormais possible de modifier les réglages des écouteurs par simple commande vocale, sans ouvrir l’application dédiée ni sortir son téléphone. On peut ainsi dire « Hey Google, augmente les basses » pour ajuster l’égaliseur. Cette fonctionnalité sera disponible aussi bien sur les Pixel Buds Pro 2 que sur les Pixel Buds 2a, modèle d’entrée de gamme lancé l’an dernier. 
Gemini permet également, selon Google, de résumer des messages ou de répondre à des textos entrants uniquement par la voix, une fonction déjà présente sur la fiche produit des Pixel Buds 2a.
Synchronisation avec la Pixel Watch et traduction élargie
Google a aussi annoncé une synchronisation entre les Pixel Buds et la Pixel Watch autour du sommeil. Typiquement, lorsque la montre détecte que son porteur s’est endormi, elle interrompt automatiquement la lecture audio, désactive les commandes tactiles des écouteurs et coupe les notifications, afin d’éviter toute interruption du repos.
Par ailleurs, la fonction de traduction en direct, déjà disponible sur les Pixel Buds Pro 2, est mise à niveau pour couvrir plus de 70 langues avec une latence réduite. Il suffit de toucher un écouteur pour activer le mode d’écoute, sans avoir à manipuler le smartphone. Selon Google, l’utilisateur peut parler dans sa propre langue tandis que le téléphone Pixel associé restitue la traduction à son interlocuteur dans la langue de ce dernier.
Enfin, les écouteurs Pixel Buds Pro 2 sont désormais disponibles dans un coloris Olive, afin de parfaitement s’harmoniser avec la teinte proposée sur les Pixel 11 Pro, 11 Pro XL et Pixel 11 Pro Fold.
Ces nouvelles fonctions ne sont pas encore actives : elles arriveront via une mise à jour logicielle gratuite déployée à partir de septembre 2026. Attention, la réduction de bruit « dynamique » reste réservée aux Pixel Buds Pro 2. Les Buds 2a se limitent, eux, aux commandes vocales Gemini et à une version plus restreinte de la traduction en direct.
Disponibilité et prix des écouteurs Google Pixel Buds Pro 2 et Buds 2a
La nouvelle teinte olive des Pixel Buds Pro 2 est commandable en ligne depuis le 12 août, avec une mise en rayon en magasin prévue à partir du 20 août selon les marchés. Le prix officiel reste fixé à 229 euros en France. Les écouteurs Buds 2a sont toujours disponibles à 149 euros.
Made by Google 2026 : toutes les annonces (Pixel 11, Pixel Watch 5 et Pixel Tag)
Pour la Made by Google 2026, la firme de Mountain View a présenté plusieurs produits : nouveaux smartphones Pixel et nouvelle montre connectée. La marque tease aussi un traqueur Bluetooth. On vous liste ici tous les sujets.
Retrouvez aussi toutes les informations concernant les précommandes des nouveaux Pixel 11.

articles.title: Everything announced at Made by Google 2026
articles.text:
Table of contents
Google held its Made by Google event on Wednesday, launching the Pixel 11 series, the Pixel Watch 5, a new Pixel Tag tracker, and an update to the Pixel Buds Pro 2. Prices went up across the phone lineup, and Google gave an official reason for it.
Here is a full breakdown of everything Google announced, prices, and what the announcement means for you if you live in Nigeria, South Africa, Kenya, or Ghana.
Where and when was it held?
Made by Google 2026 took place on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, in New York City. The keynote started at 6:00 PM ET, which is 3:00 PM PT and 11:00 PM WAT for viewers in West Africa.
Trevor Noah hosted the show, taking over from Jimmy Fallon, who hosted in 2025. The event drew guests such as Alex Cooper, Stephen Curry, Steven Gerrard, and singer PinkPantheress, who closed the night with a performance.
Google published the specs and pricing for its new devices about eight hours before the keynote started. By the time the show went live, most of the announcements were already public. The event served more as a live celebration of the launch than as a place where new information was dropped.
Everything Google announced at Made by Google 2026
Phones
Google unveiled four new phones: the Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro XL, and Pixel 11 Pro Fold. All four run on the new Tensor G6 chip, built on a 2nm process.
1. Pixel 11
- 6.3-inch display with up to 120Hz refresh rate and 3,000 nits peak brightness
- Tensor G6 chip with 12GB RAM and 256GB storage as the new base storage tier
- A 48MP main camera, plus 13MP ultrawide and 10.8MP telephoto lenses with 5x zoom
- 4,985mAh battery with 30W wired charging and 25W wireless charging
- Comes in Frost, Obsidian, Hibiscus, and Pistachio
- Priced from $899, on sale August 20
2. Pixel 11 Pro
- 6.3-inch display with 3,600 nits peak brightness
- 12GB RAM on the 256GB model, 16GB on the 512GB and 1TB models
- 50MP wide, 48MP ultrawide, 48MP telephoto with 5x optical zoom, and a 42MP selfie camera
- 4,850mAh battery
- Priced from $1,099
3. Pixel 11 Pro XL
- 6.8-inch display, same 3,600 nits peak brightness as the Pro
- Same camera setup as the Pro
- 5,115mAh battery with 45W wired charging
- Priced from $1,299
4. Pixel 11 Pro Fold
- 8-inch inner screen and 6.5-inch outer screen, both rated at 3,600 nits
- 16GB RAM across every storage tier
- 4,750mAh battery, thinner and lighter than last year’s Fold at 10.1mm and 239g
- Priced from $1,899, up $100 from last year
Some reports expected the Pro Fold to slip to October, following last year’s release pattern. Google confirmed all four phones ship together on August 20.
Why prices went up
Every phone in the Pixel 11 lineup costs $100 more than its Pixel 10 equivalent. Google gave a direct reason for this. In an interview with 9to5Google in July, Google’s VP of Devices and Services, Shakil Barkat, called it a supplier-driven memory crisis. He pointed to data showing the price of 1GB of mobile RAM jumped from $2.80 in 2025 to $12 in 2026. He said he has never seen memory prices rise this fast.
This lines up with wider trends across the phone industry. Research firm IDC expects global smartphone shipments to drop by close to 14% in 2026, the steepest fall in over ten years, while average phone prices climb to a record $523.
Wearables
The Pixel Watch 5 keeps the same design as the Pixel Watch 4 but upgrades what is inside it. It runs on a Snapdragon W5 Gen 2 chip, with RAM bumped up to 3GB and storage doubled to 64GB.
Health tracking receives several updates, including improved strength and HIIT tracking, breathing emergency detection, blood pressure trend monitoring, and insulin resistance trends. Google also says the watch now tracks running and cycling routes twice as accurately as before.
The watch runs Gemini Intelligence and supports offline Gemini commands. It comes in Matte Black, Polished Silver, Satin Pyrite, and Champagne Gold (41mm only).
Pricing starts at $399 for the 41mm model and $429 for the 45mm model, both up from the Pixel Watch 4. A Steph Curry Edition costs $579. All models go on sale August 20.
Audio
Google gave the Pixel Buds Pro 2 a new Olive colour option at the same $229 price, but the update goes beyond colour. A software upgrade coming in September adds Dynamic ANC, which adjusts noise cancellation as the earbuds shift in your ear, and Gemini voice controls that let you say things like turn up the bass.
The update also brings sleep tracking sync with the Pixel Watch and expands Live Translate to more languages. Google did not announce a Pixel Buds Pro 3 at this event.
Laptops
If you were waiting for news on Googlebook, Google’s laptop platform built to replace the Chromebook, this event did not deliver it. It did not get a demo or even a mention on stage.
Google first announced Googlebook back in May 2026, saying the first laptops would arrive from Acer, Asus, Dell, HP, and Lenovo in the fall. That timeline has not changed, and neither has the operating system’s status. Google told The Verge that Aluminium OS is only a codename for now, and the real name will come later in the year.
The next likely moment for a fuller Googlebook reveal is IFA Berlin, running September 4 to 8. Until then, treat anything about Googlebook specs or pricing as unconfirmed.
Software and AI
Every new Pixel phone runs Android 17 and comes with seven years of software and security updates.
The Tensor G6 chip brings a faster on-device AI system through Gemini Nano 4, which Google says runs up to 3.5 times faster while using less battery. On the camera side, a new feature called Magic Capture uses the chip to scan hundreds of frames and automatically picks the best shots. A new Camera Looks feature adds film-style filters, and Instant Night Sight cuts down low-light shot times.
Gemini Intelligence also picked up new tricks across the phone, including a Gboard feature that cleans up rambling voice dictation and a proactive assistant that can complete small tasks on its own. Google added American Sign Language support to Live Transcribe in Gboard as well.
Buyers of the Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL get six months of Google AI Pro included, which comes with expanded Gemini access and extra cloud storage.
Pixel Tag
Google also launched its own item tracker to compete with Apple’s AirTag. Pixel Tag costs $29 for a single unit or $99 for a four-pack, and it uses UWB and Bluetooth for precise location finding within about 50 meters. The battery is replaceable and should last more than a year. Pixel Tag ships November 11, 2026.
Pricing and availability
Here is what the new Pixel 11 lineup costs across a few major markets.
1. United States
- Pixel 11: $899 / $1,020
- Pixel 11 Pro: $1,099 / $1,220 / $1,450
- Pixel 11 Pro XL: $1,299 / $1,420 / $1,650
- Pixel 11 Pro Fold: $1,899 / $2,020 / $2,250
2. United Kingdom
- Pixel 11: £880 / £1,000
- Pixel 11 Pro: £1,080 / £1,200 / £1,430
- Pixel 11 Pro XL: £1,280 / £1,400 / £1,630
- Pixel 11 Pro Fold: £1,800 / £1,920 / £2,150
3. European Union
- Pixel 11: €1,000 / €1,130
- Pixel 11 Pro: €1,200 / €1,330 / €1,590
- Pixel 11 Pro XL: €1,400 / €1,530 / €1,790
- Pixel 11 Pro Fold: €2,000 / €2,130 / €2,390
Google confirmed launch markets covering North America, Europe, Australia, Japan, and Taiwan. Pre-orders opened on August 12, with phones and the watch shipping August 20.
4. Africa and Nigeria availability
Nigeria, South Africa, Kenya, and Ghana still have no official Google Store or authorised Pixel retailer. That has not changed with this launch.
If you want a Pixel 11 in Nigeria, your best bet is a grey-market importer. Outlets like Jumia Nigeria, Slot Nigeria, Konga, and Jiji are the usual channels for bringing in Pixel phones once they launch abroad. For context, the previous generation Pixel 9 Pro XL sold for between ₦1,180,000 and ₦1,250,000 on Jumia Nigeria, with used or UK-imported units going for less on Jiji.
Expect Pixel 11 units to land in Nigeria a few weeks after the US launch, priced at or above the US retail price once you factor in import duty, VAT, clearing fees, and shipping costs. You also won’t get a local warranty on an imported unit, so buy from a seller you trust.
Release dates at a glance
| Product | Release Date | Starting Price (US) | 
| Pixel 11 | August 20, 2026 | $899 | 
| Pixel 11 Pro | August 20, 2026 | $1,099 | 
| Pixel 11 Pro XL | August 20, 2026 | $1,299 | 
| Pixel 11 Pro Fold | August 20, 2026 | $1,899 | 
| Pixel Watch 5 (41mm) | August 20, 2026 | $399 | 
| Pixel Watch 5 (45mm) | August 20, 2026 | $429 | 
| Pixel Watch 5 Steph Curry Edition | September 3, 2026 | $579 | 
| Pixel Buds Pro 2 (Olive) | August 12, 2026 | $229 | 
| Pixel Tag | November 11, 2026 | $29 |
